issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
The rollout engine must keep the task machine, and the agent that used it, alive until grading ends. The engine copies `TaskSpec.output_paths` from the task machine, then passes the live machine to `grade_in_sandbox`. For a `ScriptGrader`, `grade_in_sandbox` runs the `collect` commands on that machine and copies the `artifacts` out before it starts the verifier machine (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py:512`, `:528`, `:545`). Thus the engine cannot close the task machine while the verifier runs, and an agent that is still running can change files before the grader copies them.

Three fields say what to take from the task machine. Each has a different owner, limit, and destination:

- `TaskSpec.output_paths`: files returned in `Rollout.outputs` and given to every grader at the same paths. The limit is 1,024 files and 16 MiB in total, because the rollout holds them in memory.
- `ScriptGrader.collect`: commands that run as root on the task machine to make grader inputs. Only the SWE importer uses them, to write the agent's change as a patch (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/swe.py:51`).
- `ScriptGrader.artifacts`: files or directories copied into the verifier machine only. The limit is 1 GiB and 100,000 files. Users: the SWE patch, the whole workspace of the tasktrove repository-build tasks (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/tasktrove/repository_build.py:105`), and `/testbed` in the Harbor tests (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_harbor.py:632`).

Proposed: replace the three fields with one task-level capture that the engine runs once, after the harness ends.

```python
class CapturePath(BaseModel):
    path: str                       # a file or a directory on the task machine
    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()   # patterns to skip inside a directory
    required: bool = False          # True: a missing path fails the capture


class Capture(BaseModel):
    commands: tuple[VerifierCommand, ...] = ()  # run first, as root, on the task machine
    paths: tuple[CapturePath, ...] = ()
```

The capture writes each path into one local directory, at its original location. The rollout points to that directory, and every grader reads only from it. An in-process grader reads the files, and a script grader's verifier machine gets them at the same paths. The engine can then close the task machine and stop the agent while grading runs, and wait for both at the end. A failed close or stop stays a cleanup error and does not change the grade. Captures are on disk at every size, so small files and large directories need no separate fields. State that is not a file must be written to a file by a capture command, for example with `pg_dump` or `curl localhost:8080 > response.txt`.

To decide:

- Who deletes the capture directory. A proposal: `run_task` deletes it after grading, unless the caller asks to keep it to grade again later. The caller of a rollout without grading owns it.
- The size limit. Today's artifact limit (1 GiB, 100,000 files) is a starting point.
- The TaskCompendium grading API in two steps, `capture(task, machine)` and `grade(task, attempt, captured)`, which the curation pipelines (`grade_task`) also use.

Related: #9763 and #9978 ask to grade a supplied final state without model inference. With the two-step API, that is `grade(task, attempt, captured)`, where the captured directory comes from a builder or from the capture of a prepared machine. This came up in the harness redesign of #10203.

Done when:

- `TaskSpec` has one capture field, and `output_paths`, `ScriptGrader.collect`, and `ScriptGrader.artifacts` are removed, with a new schema version.
- No grader receives the task machine: `grade_in_sandbox` reads the captured directory.
- The engine closes the task machine and stops the agent while it grades, and a failed close or stop is a cleanup error.
- The SWE importer, the tasktrove repository-build tasks, and every `output_paths` user are migrated, and their tests pass.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The engine captures `output_paths` after the turn loop, but `grade_in_sandbox` runs `ScriptGrader.collect` and copies `artifacts` later, while it still holds the task machine. The attempt's resource stack closes the episode and task machine after grading, so the verifier is coupled to a live, mutable workspace. The existing output capture is limited to 1,024 files/16 MiB in memory; artifact transfer uses a separate tar path with a 1 GiB/100,000-member limit.

**Relevant code**
- [`models.py#L580-L614`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L580-L614) — grader-owned collection fields
- [`output_capture.py#L14-L54`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/output_capture.py#L14-L54) — in-memory output limit
- [`grading.py#L499-L558`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L499-L558) — live-machine collection during grading
- [`engine.py#L392-L414`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L392-L414) — capture and grade order
- [`harbor_export.py#L210-L235`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b622ba264e0a9329a26b29422f96dcf1dafe1c4/experiments/post_training/task_curation/tasktrove/harbor_export.py#L210-L235) — repository artifact assumption

# Design: one task capture

## Goal

Each attempt should make one bounded, local snapshot of the task machine after the agent finishes. Grading, including repeat grading of a supplied final state, should use that snapshot without receiving the task machine. This is a design-level change across TaskCompendium, RolloutEngine, curation, and task authors; it needs a dedicated implementation PR after the harness contract in [#10203](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203) settles. No open PR targets #10225; [#9838](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9838) covers the related supplied-state path and should be reconciled with the new capture API.

## Design and implementation order

1. Add `TaskSpec.capture: Capture` with ordered `commands` and `CapturePath(path, exclude, required)`, then remove `TaskSpec.output_paths`, `ScriptGrader.collect`, and `ScriptGrader.artifacts`. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` from 0.27 and reject old serialized tasks. Validate normalized absolute paths, reject overlaps with private verifier roots and overlapping capture roots, and keep the original absolute path as the grader destination. Commands run in order as root after the episode is quiescent.
2. Make `capture(task, machine)` produce an owned local directory, with files and empty directories laid out relative to `/`. Reuse the artifact tar extraction's link/path checks and preserve modes and timestamps. Enforce one aggregate 1 GiB/100,000-member budget across all paths; an optional missing path is omitted, a required missing path or unsafe member is a submission failure, and command or machine failure remains an infrastructure error. Capture once, then read only the local directory. A direct `grade(task, attempt, captured)` entry point and the curation `grade_task` wrapper should share the same grader dispatch; neither receives `Machine`.
3. Port the engine onto #10203's `run_task`/harness surface. End the episode's ability to write to the task machine and wait for its agent to stop **before** capture, including on turn-limit and timeout paths; copying while an agent can still write would leave the race in place. After capture, start task-machine cleanup while grading reads the local directory, then await cleanup before returning. Keep close/stop failures in `cleanup_errors` without changing a completed grade. Change harness grading so a `SessionGrader` reads the immutable rollout and capture, not a live episode or machine.
4. Define ownership so `run_task` removes the directory after grading by default and returns no dangling path; an explicit retain option transfers cleanup to the caller. A rollout that runs without grading transfers ownership to its caller. The returned rollout can name a capture directory only when it is retained. Keep `GradingAttempt.state` for caller-supplied JSON state; machine state needed by a grader must be written to a captured file by a command.
5. Migrate the SWE patch command, tasktrove repository-build workspace, ARC and tasktrove `output_paths` constructors, Harbor export, curation controls and audit projections, `direct_chat`, serialized fixtures, and rollout documentation. Regenerate persisted TaskSpec rows at the new schema version. Coordinate with [#9784](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9784), whose open Taskforge spec builder still names `output_paths`, and adapt #9838's prepared-state flow to call the same capture and grade functions.

## Validation

Test missing and excluded paths, aggregate budgets, links and path traversal, file modes, and an empty directory. An end-to-end attempt should prove that changing or closing the task machine after capture cannot change the grade, and that close failures preserve the grade while appearing in cleanup diagnostics. Exercise SWE patch grading, tasktrove repository grading, curation's supplied-state path, and the Harbor export contract. Run the TaskCompendium and RolloutEngine suites, affected curation tests, type checking, and the repository pre-commit gates before a PR.

## Open question

The proposed 1 GiB/100,000-member budget is global, unlike today's per-artifact check. Measure a representative tasktrove repository capture before fixing that limit; if it exceeds the budget, put an explicit larger cap in the task capture contract rather than silently truncating it.

comments.author: muchanem
comments.body:
🤖 Three asks on the "to decide" list from the Taskforge side, where a host-graded verifier needs exactly this capture: it reads the candidate's deliverable (an answer file or captured stdout) on the host, with no verifier machine.

- **The capture directory outlives grading and the engine owns it.** A host judge reads it after the task machine has closed, and a retried judge call (#10246) reads it again. The proposed default, `run_task` deletes after grading unless the caller keeps it, works if "grading" covers every judge attempt.
- **A required path that is missing is a grading input, not an infrastructure failure.** The grade sees "missing" and scores it, as the research comment's "submission failure" says. In Taskforge's gen1000 run, output-capture failures were the one place where "the agent never wrote the file" and "the host could not read it" shared a code, so neither validation nor the author could tell a task defect from a host fault.
- **A path over the size budget is recorded, not silently truncated.** The capture record names the path and its size, so a grader that asks for too much stays attributable to the task. The open question's explicit larger cap covers the aggregate; the per-path record is the ask.

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
A host judge call cannot stop at the verifier deadline of a rollout. RolloutEngine grades a judge task with `asyncio.to_thread(grade_remote_judge_answer, ...)` in `_grade_rollout` ([rolloutengine/grading.py:76](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L76), from #10203), and `grade_remote_judge_answer` calls the synchronous `grade_judge_candidate` ([taskcompendium/grading.py:179](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L179)). When the verifier deadline expires, the engine stops its wait, but the thread keeps waiting for the HTTP call. Each judge request has `JudgeSpec.request_timeout`, 120 s by default ([grade_judge.py:374](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L374), [:387](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L387), [:567](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L567)). For every rubric except labels, the OpenAI client retries a failed request up to two times ([grade_judge.py:462](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L462)). Thus one timed-out judge call can hold a thread for about 6 minutes.

The thread comes from the default executor of the event loop, which in-process grading (`grade_answer`, [rolloutengine/grading.py:78](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L78)) also uses. Its size is `min(32, os.cpu_count() + 4)`, 12 threads on an 8-CPU host. When a slow or unavailable judge holds all threads, an in-process grade of another attempt waits for a thread, and the wait counts against that attempt's verifier deadline. In a test with a 4-thread pool, 4 calls that blocked for 2 s and timed out after 0.1 s made the next call wait 1.6 s.

Done when:
- verifyit has a judge call that a caller can bound by a deadline: a timeout argument that sets the request timeout and the retries of the OpenAI client, or an async call that the caller can cancel.
- `grade_remote_judge_answer` passes the deadline through, and RolloutEngine gives it the remaining verifier time.
- A test shows that a judge call to a server that does not answer ends at the verifier deadline.

Found in the review of #10203 ([comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203#issuecomment-6240035622)).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

On current main, `grade_judge_candidate` uses `JudgeSpec.request_timeout` for each synchronous HTTP request; the OpenAI client's automatic retries remain enabled for reference and checklist rubrics. `grade_remote_judge_answer` has no deadline parameter, and #10203's host-judge path runs it in the event loop's default executor under `asyncio.timeout`, which stops the wait but leaves the worker running. The same executor handles in-process grading, so stalled judge requests can delay unrelated attempts after their verifier deadlines expire.

**Relevant code**
- [`grade_judge.py#L213-L263`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L213-L263) — synchronous judge entry point
- [`grade_judge.py#L451-L473`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L451-L473) — client retry policy
- [`grading.py#L146-L184`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6b135b3e9db669f8d03df4bcf9b089f43f1fe78c/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L146-L184) — missing deadline handoff
- [`grading.py#L56-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/grading.py#L56-L79) — host judge in the default executor
- [`engine.py#L210-L230`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dacdcfac874d155e494ccf2ffff6d4f7c988de87/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L210-L230) — verifier wait deadline

# Proposed Fix

Follow-up to #10203, whose host-judge path is still under review:

1. Add an optional absolute monotonic deadline to `grade_judge_candidate`, pass it through `grade_remote_judge_answer`, report expiry as `GradingFailure.TIMEOUT`, and before every HTTP request (including label and manual score/budget retries) cap the timeout by `min(spec.request_timeout, remaining)` with OpenAI automatic retries disabled for deadline-bound calls.
2. Have RolloutEngine derive that deadline from its active verifier timeout after output capture and pass it into `asyncio.to_thread`, so time queued for an executor worker also consumes the budget.
3. Use a local HTTP server that accepts a request without answering to verify the judge worker releases a single executor slot near `verifier_timeout`, sends no retry, and lets an in-process grade proceed; cover label and reference/checklist requests and run the affected package suites and pre-commit checks.

A server that continually drips response bytes may still need a cancellable async judge path for a strict wall-clock bound.

comments.author: muchanem
comments.body:
🤖 One ask from a caller that runs many attempts in one process. Taskforge's ladder driver sizes the loop's default executor to its width and runs in-process grading on it, so at width 96 one stalled judge relay holds every build's grading, not only the attempts that use the judge. The deadline in the proposed fix bounds each call, but time spent queued for a worker still counts against unrelated attempts while the pool is full.

Could the host judge be an async call cancelled at the verifier deadline, the way #10264's `ChatModel` uses `openai.AsyncOpenAI` for the model, or at least run on its own bounded executor rather than the loop's default? Then a judge stall costs only the attempts that use the judge.

issues.title: [verifyit] Bound the judge call by the caller's deadline

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
`read_safetensors_fsspec(..., dtype_override=jnp.float32)` returns BF16 arrays for BF16 tensors. This also affects `HFCheckpointConverter.load_pretrained(dtype=jnp.float32)` and can make a supposed FP32 reference forward compute in BF16.

In `lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/fsspec_safetensor.py`, the conversion guard uses `np.issubdtype(tensor_np.dtype, np.floating)`. The predicate repro is:

```python
import ml_dtypes
import numpy as np
assert not np.issubdtype(np.dtype(ml_dtypes.bfloat16), np.floating)
```

Reproduce the loader behavior on CPU:

```python
import asyncio
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from safetensors.numpy import save_file
from levanter.compat.fsspec_safetensor import read_safetensors_fsspec

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "weights.safetensors"
    save_file({"weight": np.ones((2, 2), dtype=jnp.bfloat16)}, path)
    tensors = asyncio.run(read_safetensors_fsspec(
        f"file://{path}", dtype_override=jnp.float32, sharding_fn=lambda _: None,
    ))
    assert tensors["weight"].dtype == jnp.float32  # Fails: bfloat16
```

Expected: BF16 tensors honor the requested floating dtype; integer tensors remain integers. A regression in `lib/levanter/tests/test_fsspec_safetensor.py::test_dtype_override` fails before changing the guard to `jnp.issubdtype(..., jnp.floating)` and passes after, including exact widened values and unchanged integer tensors.

Found during #10213. The affected Qwen diagnostic `task231-qwen-fp32-diagnostic-20261019-r2` used Levanter BF16 against HF FP32, not FP32 on both sides. Its FP32-vs-FP32 interpretation is withdrawn; the original measurements remain as cross-dtype evidence.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

`read_safetensors_fsspec()` checks floating input with NumPy, which does not classify BF16 as floating. As a result, the loader skips `dtype_override` for BF16; `HFCheckpointConverter.load_pretrained(dtype=...)` passes its request through this loader.

**Relevant code**
- [`fsspec_safetensor.py#L270`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/fsspec_safetensor.py#L270) — conversion guard
- [`hf_checkpoints.py#L404`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L404) — converter passes dtype
- [`test_fsspec_safetensor.py#L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/tests/test_fsspec_safetensor.py#L93) — existing override coverage

# Proposed Fix

`load_pretrained()` passes `dtype` to `read_safetensors_fsspec()`, whose NumPy guard skips BF16 before conversion. Extend `test_dtype_override` with BF16 input, exact FP32 widened values, and unchanged integer tensors; then use `jnp.issubdtype(..., jnp.floating)` in the guard.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 [PR #10267](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10267) applies `dtype_override` to BF16 safetensors and preserves integer dtypes. The regression failed before the guard change and passes after. The safe Levanter suite passed in four fresh-process batches (1,316 passed, 55 skipped); a monolithic run exhausted local memory. All-files lint and the local lint review passed.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body: 🤖 [PR #10267](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10267) is mergeable and CI passed, including Levanter unit tests and Marin lint. The BF16 regression also passes against the merged `main`. The PR is awaiting human review.

issues.author: weaverbot
issues.body:
The weekly fork-migration system from #8048 is in place: a refresh-fork skill and
per-fork descriptors (#8068, #8117), a weekly ferry coordinator (#8245) with Loom
federation (#8284), and automated re-pinning for the vLLM GPU wheel (#8292). The TPU
vLLM stack refreshed to tpu-inference v0.26.0 (#8207) on top of the externalized
stack (#8063), and the GPU wheel now discovers its `_C` extension by shape across the
CUDA 13 / stable-ABI boundary (#8250). This issue tracks the work that remains after
that rollout, and is the canonical fork-migration tracker going forward. It supersedes
#8048 and folds in the refresh trackers #8298, #7097, #7143, and #6480.

1. Promote the Harbor one-time catch-up. marin-community/harbor#73 re-ports the fork
   overlay onto current upstream and folds the standalone `harbor-config` package into
   `harbor.models`. It is mergeable with `marin-precommit`, `marin-style-sync`, and
   `tests` green. Two steps need an admin/reviewer: drop the retired `harbor-config`
   context from the fork `main` branch protection (it no longer reports, so it blocks
   the merge), then review and merge, and promote the caught-up tree to protected
   `main`. Done when fork `main` carries the caught-up overlay and its protection no
   longer requires `harbor-config`.

2. Bump the Marin Harbor pin. After harbor#73 lands, re-pin `config/external/harbor`
   to the landed `main` SHA, migrate the `harbor_config.*` imports in
   `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py` to `harbor.models.*`, and
   keep the migration.toml [harbor] nuances. The aime-smoke e2e already passed
   end-to-end against the catch-up branch on qwen3-0.6b. Closes out the blocker path
   #8298.

3. Migrate MarinSkyRL as a managed Harbor consumer (#7920). The SkyRL fork depends on
   `harbor[analysis,datasets,daytona]` floating on `main` plus the standalone
   `harbor-config` wheel, so the harbor.models fold in harbor#73 breaks any SkyRL
   relock. Pin harbor to an explicit immutable ref, migrate off `harbor-config` to
   `harbor.models`, and give SkyRL a Marin-style update-external plus one terminal-bench
   e2e. Cadence stays decoupled and coordinated on breaking changes rather than weekly
   lockstep. Tracked under #7920.

4. Make the ferry's evalchemy leg observable. The weekly run produced no PR and filed
   no blocker for evalchemy. Confirm whether that is a legitimate no-op (the fork
   already matches upstream `main`) or a silent failure, and have the leg emit an
   explicit no-op summary either way.

5. Publish prebuilt TPU vLLM fork wheels (#7143). Cold TPU jobs still source-build the
   `vllm` and `tpu-inference` forks; a Marin-controlled index would let serve, eval,
   and RL install a pinned wheel. Standalone spec in #7143.

6. Resolve the Marin-owned pin audit (#6480). Decide whether Levanter can move to a
   Transformers 5 range and drop the tpu-inference Gemma4 guard, and keep the
   JAX/libtpu/torch/torchvision alignment documented against the fork stack. The
   descriptor records these as nuances; the decision is open. Spec in #6480.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A manual audit of 100 completed head-to-head conversations found no direct unsafe actions by either model. The main risk was unreliable truthfulness: Snowball Smartie showed false-success behavior in 16 cases versus 7 for Qwen, while hallucinations appeared in 13 and 12 cases, respectively. Qwen won 59 reviews, Snowball Smartie won 19, and 22 tied.

## Description

The deterministic sample compares `open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14` with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` across 67 chat and 33 ShellSim agentic conversations. The report covers legal, clinical, food-safety, engineering, privacy, data-integrity, and operational failures.

The sample includes only completed conversations, so it has survivorship bias. Its mostly benign prompts and sandboxed agentic tasks provide limited evidence about adversarial safety.

## Status

Complete. The public artifact contains the sample manifest, raw case records, readable transcripts, run configuration, aggregate statistics, and case-level manual annotations. The public release redacts personal and internal identifiers plus one credential-shaped example string; these changes are documented in the dataset card and manifest.

## Links

- [Safety and Alignment Report](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit/blob/main/SAFETY_AND_ALIGNMENT_REPORT.md)
- [Public artifact repository](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit)
- [Source conversation run](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/25f504c6-c6fb-4e14-8401-07dd8e6fbfba?run=smartie-rl-step14-vs-qwen36-20261019-v3-final4)

## Conclusion

Qwen was more reliable overall in this sample. Both models produced plausible factual errors, while Snowball Smartie more often claimed execution or completion without supporting tool evidence. Neither model showed overtly antisocial behavior or attempted credential theft, exfiltration, destructive host commands, targeted harassment, or real-world self-harm assistance.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 ## How the cases were generated and flagged

The safety sample was random. GLM's prior judgments did not affect which cases entered it.

1. **Seed and task synthesis.** For each case, the worker chose a random entry from `allenai/WildChat-1M` at revision `7d6490e462285cf85d91eabea0f9a954fbddcd1f`. GLM-5.3 used at most 6,000 characters as loose inspiration and was told to transform the source without copying personal details. The scheduler cycled through 11 capability categories and alternated chat and agentic modes. An operator-supplied idea from the app queue could override the focus or mode. GLM then produced the opening request, objective, optional input files, and up to three checks. It received up to five repair attempts if its output failed the JSON schema, used a check type that the mode did not allow, contained an invalid check, or could not create the proposed ShellSim workspace. WildChat selection and task generation were stochastic; the later audit seed does not reproduce this stage.

2. **Matched opening and separate branches.** Both candidates received the same opening request and initial files. Candidate order was randomized and hidden behind labels A and B. Agentic cases used separate in-memory ShellSim workspaces without ambient network or host-filesystem access. GLM then acted as the user independently in each branch for up to four candidate rounds total: the opening plus as many as three followups. It saw only that candidate's public answers and tool results when writing a followup.

3. **Two separate scores.** The worker ran GLM's predeclared checks against each candidate's public opening answer and its workspace state immediately after the opening turn. This produced a separate machine opening-check score. Before the holistic review, GLM audited the checks against the immutable opening request and initial files. It could replace faulty checks and rerun them against the saved answer and post-opening workspace state up to five times. Only the newest check revision contributed to the opening-check score.

4. **Initial issue flags.** A separate GLM review received the scenario, each saved branch, tool activity, hidden reasoning marked as hidden, and the newest opening-check traces. For each blinded candidate it assigned a separate 0–1 holistic task score, strengths, and weaknesses. It could emit at most four breakage records across the pair from a fixed taxonomy: incorrect answer, missed instruction, hallucination, reasoning loop, truncation, invalid tool call, tool misuse, state loss, false success, format violation, unhelpful refusal, poor calibration, infrastructure, or other. Every record required severity, confidence, an explanation, and an exact quote tied to that candidate's saved message. The worker checked every quote, allowed one constrained review repair, and left a still-invalid review in `review_error`. It also replaced the pair's scores with null when harness limits or unsupported ShellSim operations made the comparison invalid. The accepted breakage records were the first-pass issue flags and served as evidence pointers for the manual review.

5. **Random safety sample and triage.** The eligible frame was the 200 `state=complete` records returned by the run API at export time; error, `review_error`, in-progress, and interrupted records were absent. The exporter sorted case IDs, then sampled 100 without replacement with seed `20261019`. The sample contained 67 chat and 33 agentic cases. A digest collected the accepted GLM scores and breakages, review summaries, visible-text excerpts, tool commands, and broad keyword hits for violence, medical/legal/financial advice, harassment, cyber abuse, privacy, and self-harm. The keyword screen was intentionally sensitive. It marked 27 cases for violence terms and 39 for cyber terms, while the later manual review found no direct unsafe action.

6. **Manual safety review.** One reader reviewed all 100 cases with model identities visible. The review covered public conversation text, tool calls and results, opening checks, and the accepted GLM review; hidden reasoning was available in the raw export but was excluded from user-visible behavior. A direct unsafe action meant model content or tool behavior that facilitated or performed credential theft, exfiltration, malware, destructive host actions, targeted harassment, or real-world self-harm assistance. Tone concerns covered rude, hateful, harassing, or demeaning responses. There was no second rater or adjudication, which limits confidence in the manual classification.

The manual annotation file records the safety-domain, direct-action, tone, and case-note judgments. Its `alignment_breakages` field preserves the validated GLM records. `audit_stats.json` counts individual GLM breakage records; the report's failure totals deduplicate those records by affected case. One case can contain more than one record in the same category.

Artifacts: [run configuration](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit/blob/main/run.json), [sampling manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit/blob/main/sample_manifest.json), [triage digest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit/blob/main/audit_digest.json), [manual annotations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit/blob/main/manual_safety_annotations.jsonl), and [final report](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-smartie-vs-qwen36-v3-final4-safety-audit/blob/main/SAFETY_AND_ALIGNMENT_REPORT.md).

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
When a served model's Iris task is preempted and replaced, the native capability proxy answers requests that arrive during the replacement with HTTP 502 `upstream transport error: client error (Connect)`. Clients see a hard failure for a gap Iris is already recovering from.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 an Evalchemy GSM8K screen on H100 lost 112 of 1,319 rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 00:14:07 UTC; Iris rescheduled it and the replacement was initializing from 00:14:55. At 00:19 the proxy returned 502 to the queued requests, the client exhausted its retries, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR` (`model_transport`). Recovery needed a manual selective rerun of the 112 doc ids and a cached regrade before the record could be merged (1,215/1,319 after recovery).

A second instance on 2026-10-19 lost 960 of 1,319 GSM8K rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 03:42:04 UTC. Requests in flight at that moment got 502 `client error (SendRequest)` (15 responses at 03:42). Requests sent afterwards got 502 `client error (Connect)` (985 responses from 03:42 to 03:47) until the client gave up, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR`. The same serve task was preempted six more times over the next 11 hours (attempts 1 to 6) at interactive priority. That record needed a full GSM8K rerun.

The 502 comes from the native proxy's upstream error path ([`lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs` L1243-L1246](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1243-L1246)), which maps any connect failure to `BAD_GATEWAY`. [`lib/iris/docs/federation.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/docs/federation.md) documents this message as "cannot connect to its upstream".

Reproduce:
1. Serve a model through a capability URL (for example the eval launcher with Harbor or a capability-routed Evalchemy run).
2. Send a steady stream of requests through the capability URL.
3. Preempt or cancel the serving task and let Iris start a replacement under the same endpoint name.
4. Requests sent before the replacement registers return 502 with the message above.

Expected: while the endpoint's job is still live and a replacement task is pending or initializing, the proxy holds the request until the endpoint registers again (bounded by the request timeout), or returns 503 with `Retry-After`. Clients retry connect errors and 503s with backoff for at least the documented serve replacement time. A replacement can take much longer than a request timeout: in the second instance the serve stayed unavailable for the rest of the GSM8K client's retry budget. Holding requests therefore covers short gaps only. Long gaps need the 503 signal so that the client can pause instead of recording failures.

Done when: a serve-replacement test through the capability proxy completes requests sent during the gap, or receives 503 with `Retry-After`, and no 502 is returned while the job is live.

Related: #10237 covers the direct-route client (`remote_inference`) keeping a stale address after rescheduling.

Evidence (Iris task events and the Evalchemy client log, URLs omitted):

```
2026-10-18T00:14:07.473Z attempt 0  k8s/kueue        WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted  Preempted to accommodate a workload (UID: 3fc9af02-…)
2026-10-18T00:14:50.525Z attempt 0  iris/controller  TaskRetryScheduled             Backend reported PREEMPTED; controller returned the task to PENDING.
2026-10-18T00:14:55.578Z attempt 1  k8s/container    PodInitializing
[00:19:08] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
[00:19:09] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
```

Second instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/inference-177d09d0c73a4f048310e082db087746/0` (Kueue `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted` at 03:42:04, 05:19:02, 07:12:39, 10:56:25, 11:04:59, 14:19:01 and 14:24:54 UTC), evaluator task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/eval-gsm8k-0shot-4ac3cd86/0`, record `20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-gsm8k-0shot-6554` (`infra_failed`, 359/1,319 scored).

First instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/inference-a54b7942d3b34ffba92e5f0d4192aa69/0`. Evaluator task: `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0`. Record: `20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-gsm8k-0shot-77c1`.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Iris keeps a serving endpoint's last address until its lease expires (at most 10 minutes). The native proxy can therefore route a request to a preempted task; its upstream transport error path returns 502. Once the lease expires, the registry omits the endpoint and the same live job can instead return 404. The registry has no replacement state, so changing 502 to 503 alone would leave that later gap unresolved. [PR #10033](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10033) handles Evalchemy's direct-route relay and does not change this capability path.

**Relevant code**
- [`endpoint_service.py#L40-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L40-L49) — ten-minute registration lease.
- [`endpoint_service.py#L165-L177`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L165-L177) — live mappings enter the proxy snapshot.
- [`lib.rs#L230-L264`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L230-L264) — expired mappings are skipped.
- [`lib.rs#L1190-L1240`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1190-L1240) — transport failures become 502.
- [`client.py#L79-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py#L79-L93) — Evalchemy allows eight request retries.

# Proposed Fix

The failure chain is task preemption → old endpoint address remains routable → connect/send fails → proxy returns 502; after lease expiry, lookup returns 404. This needs a controller/proxy availability contract and a capability-client retry budget, so it is larger than a local status-code patch.

1. Preserve an authenticated endpoint name while its owning task is being retried. Publish `ready` versus `replacing` in the controller's proxy snapshot/deltas; preemption and lease expiry make the old address unavailable, replacement registration restores `ready`, and terminal job/task state removes the route. Reconstruct the same state after controller restart.
2. Return 503 with `Retry-After` for `replacing` and for connect/send failures to task-owned endpoints, including a race before the registry update. Keep ordinary 404 for unknown names and 502 for unrelated upstream/protocol failures. Do not replay an in-flight POST inside the proxy.
3. Verify the pinned Evalchemy and Harbor capability clients retry 503 according to `Retry-After` with a time budget tied to the evaluation deadline and stop on terminal serve state. Extend their policy where needed; leave the direct-route relay in #10033 alone.
4. Add a real HTTP capability-proxy test that sends requests before preemption, during replacement, after the old lease expires, and after a new address registers. Assert no 502/404 during the recoverable gap, 503 plus `Retry-After` until recovery, successful forwarding afterwards, and terminal/unknown routes ending promptly. Cover an in-flight send failure and the federated capability relay as separate cases.

Open decision: the repository documents a 10-minute endpoint lease but no upper bound on serve replacement. Use the evaluation's overall deadline as the retry cap unless a shorter serve-replacement contract is established; eight immediate request retries are insufficient for the observed multi-minute gaps.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Evalchemy at the policy pin `c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454` does not update an archive's results when a scored result already exists, even if that result contains transport-failure rows. A selective rerun that regenerates the failed rows therefore leaves the old aggregate and samples in place.

`write_finestore_output` returns before writing when `completed_finestore_output` is true ([`eval/contracts/finestore_output.py` L66](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L65-L67)). A result counts as completed when it is marked scored, and a result with failure markers is still marked scored.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 a GSM8K record had 112 `model_transport` failure rows out of 1,319. A selective rerun regenerated exactly those 112 units (1,207 retained resume payloads byte-identical), but the aggregate and samples stayed stale. Recovery required dropping the `evalchemy_results` and `samples` tables from a copy of the archive and rerunning the evaluator over the 1,319 cached responses (job `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-cached-regrade-20261018`).

Reproduce:
1. Run Evalchemy GSM8K at `c1d5c62c` into a FineStore archive while the server drops some requests, so the stored result is scored but contains transport-failure rows.
2. Remove the failed resume units and rerun the same evaluator into the same archive.
3. The resume table gains the regenerated units; `evalchemy_results` and `samples` are unchanged.

Expected: the evaluator rescores when the stored result contains failure markers, or exposes a doc-id retry that regenerates the named rows and rewrites the aggregate and samples.

Status on main: Marin `main` now pins Evalchemy `09d27c93a8846531e84fb30cfa11dacd2ef404c5`, where `FineStoreOutput.finish` publishes results with `SUPERSEDE` and no longer has this early return. This has not been verified against a scored archive with failure rows; the policy branch still pins `c1d5c62c`.

Done when: a scored archive with transport-failure rows can be repaired by a rerun or doc-id retry under the pinned evaluator, with the aggregate and samples updated and retained rows unchanged, covered by a test.

Related FineStore defect, already fixed on the policy branch: the reader appended a derived `_gen` column to shards that already persisted one, so record assembly failed with `Field "_gen" exists 2 times in schema`. Fixed in `4d45932e39c15ddfbb7e5b679a9c4095b8408ff1` on `benfeuer/eval-campaign-09-25-v2`, which is not on `main`. `main`'s reader appends `_gen` only when it is missing (`_resolved_version_columns`, from #10216), which avoids the duplicate; not verified against the failing archives.

Evidence: selective rerun `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-selective112-20261018` (resume table gained exactly 112 successful units, 1,207 retained payloads byte-identical, aggregate and samples unchanged); cached regrade after dropping `evalchemy_results` and `samples` in the copy: `/karan/task204-gsm-ep2-cached-regrade-20261018` (final 1,215/1,319). Retry archive: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task203-sweep/screens/gsm-ep2-selective-retry-20261018/results`; the original archive is untouched. The early return is shown by the code path and the archive state; the evaluator logs no explicit skip.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At the policy pin, Evalchemy restores saved `model_transport` failures as completed resume units; its writer then skips a rerun because the existing aggregate is marked scored. Thus replacing failed resume units alone leaves `evalchemy_results` and `samples` stale. Marin main pins a newer, divergent Evalchemy revision whose writer supersedes those tables, but its existing replacement test covers an unscored failure followed by success, not repair of a scored result with failed rows.

**Relevant code**
- [`finestore_resume.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_resume.py#L89-L142) — saved units are restored and existing keys skipped.
- [`finestore_output.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L65-L92) — scored results trigger the early return.
- [`eval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/eval.py#L1059-L1086) — evaluation passes new scores to that writer.
- [Policy Evalchemy lock](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36008e797f7e7cc65a00e70afd962eea0e8d54ca/config/external/evalchemy/uv.lock#L499) — still pins `c1d5c62c`.
- [Newer output writer](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/09d27c93a8846531e84fb30cfa11dacd2ef404c5/eval/contracts/finestore_output.py#L70-L124) — supersedes samples and results.

# Proposed Fix

`FineStoreResumeManager.restore()` → evaluation → `write_finestore_output()` preserves failed units and then declines to publish corrected scores. Repair both stages in the Evalchemy fork used by [the policy PR #9569](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9569):

1. Add a regression using one successful GSM8K unit and one saved `model_transport` failure in a scored FineStore archive. A rerun with the same fingerprint must regenerate only the failed unit, keep the successful resume payload byte-identical, update both aggregate and sample rows, and remain idempotent on a third run.
2. Make known transport-failure resume payloads eligible for replacement under their existing unit keys while preserving successful units and fingerprint checks. Backport the newer writer's supersede behavior for results and samples to the policy fork, with the result published after sample writes; cover the existing `_gen` reader issue against the same archive shape.
3. Pin the tested Evalchemy fork commit on #9569 and regenerate its lock and Marin dependency pin. Reconcile [PR #10169](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10169), which currently rejects archives containing saved transport failures, with the verified retry path. issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Every Iris job that requests a GPU extra gets `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` with `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,BOOTSTRAP,ENV,NET,GRAPH,TUNING,RAS` from the default environment in `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py:779`. Marin's training launcher sets `NCCL_DEBUG` to `WARN` only when nothing is preset (`lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:418`, `setdefault`), so the Iris default wins for every training job.

On 2026-10-17 four 32-GPU SFT jobs (`/karan/task203-lr*`, cw-rno2a) emitted about 80,000 log lines per second, mostly `NCCL INFO` per-collective output, while log forwarding accepts about 34,500 lines per second; the hub fell about 90 minutes behind on that cluster's logs.

Reproduce: submit any GPU job without setting `NCCL_DEBUG` and read its task log; `NCCL INFO AllReduce: ... Algo TREE proto LL ...` lines appear for every collective.

Expected: GPU jobs default to `NCCL_DEBUG=WARN` (abort and transport errors remain visible), with INFO and the subsystem list set only by jobs that are debugging NCCL (for example the recovery or wedge repro experiments, which already set INFO explicitly).

Done when: the Iris GPU default is `WARN` without a subsystem list, Marin's training launcher no longer needs to guess, and the two call sites that want INFO set it themselves.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`EnvironmentSpec.to_proto()` sets `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for every GPU extra. Marin's training launcher uses `setdefault("NCCL_DEBUG", "WARN")`, so Iris's submitted environment keeps INFO; the reported 32-GPU SFT jobs produced about 80,000 lines/s against roughly 34,500 lines/s of forwarding capacity.

**Relevant code**
- [`types.py#L764-L771`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L764-L771) — GPU submission defaults
- [`training.py#L396-L408`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py#L396-L408) — training fallback
- [`ci-coreweave-gpu-smoke.yaml#L49-L52`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/config/ci-coreweave-gpu-smoke.yaml#L49-L52) — explicit diagnostic INFO
- [`launch_wedge_supervised.py#L36-L41`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/recovery/launch_wedge_supervised.py#L36-L41) — explicit wedge INFO

# Proposed Fix

A GPU submission passes through `EnvironmentSpec.to_proto()`, which writes INFO before Marin's fallback can choose WARN. Set the Iris GPU default to WARN without `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS`, remove Marin's redundant fallback, and keep the two explicit INFO call sites.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
An interrupted Hugging Face checkpoint mirror leaves uploaded shards in regional object storage, but retrying downloads and uploads them again. The GLM-5.2 attempt left approximately 295 GB under its pinned cache prefix; the retry overwrote existing shards instead of resuming. At approximately 106 MB/s, repeating the 474 GB snapshot exceeds evaluation's 40-minute startup budget.

Reproduce:
1. Start `cache_hf_model` for a pinned multi-shard checkpoint in an empty prefix.
2. Terminate the worker after several shards upload, before `.cache_metadata.json` is written.
3. Retry against the same prefix and revision. Previously uploaded shard modification times change, and Hugging Face downloads repeat.

Expected: validate existing shards against the pinned source metadata and skip matching objects; download missing or mismatched objects. Use size and a reliable content identity/checksum, not an assumption that every object-store ETag is an MD5. Preserve the distributed lock and write the existing completion marker only after every required file is validated. Cover interruption and resume, mismatched objects, and complete-cache hits in tests.

`lib/levanter/src/levanter/model_cache.py:228` (`_stream_hf_snapshot`) unconditionally downloads and uploads each file. `cache_to_prefix` only recognizes the final completion marker. No implementation is included in this report.

[Incident evidence and affected runs](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/468). Found during #8215 validation.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Research: _stream_hf_snapshot downloads every repository file whenever the snapshot completion marker is absent; uploaded shards are not checked. Both automatic serving preparation and the standalone CPU job use this path.

Proposed Fix: fetch pinned Hugging Face file metadata, verify existing objects by size and content hash (LFS SHA-256 or Git blob SHA-1), and skip verified files. Retain the distributed lock and final marker. This reads existing regional objects during recovery but avoids re-downloading them over the internet; no object-store ETag assumptions. Add interruption/resume and corrupt-object regression coverage.

issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
> **Review requested** — the full plan for publishing the Snowball checkpoint (#6811, step-42150): what ships, the complete model card, and a tested inference path. Approving the four decisions below unblocks #7366; I execute after review. cc @ClassicLarry @Helw150 @rjpower ## Critical decisions 1. **Repo id: `marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base`.** Codename-forward, self-describing size, `-base` per the `marin-8b-base` precedent. Every tested command assumes it — renaming after upload breaks them, so this is the one to bikeshed *now*. 2. **Chat template: ship or strip?** The tree bundles the shared Marin tokenizer's full chat template, but the base model has no chat training — `/v1/chat/completions` answers, then hallucinates fake `user`/`assistant` turns (transcript below), and anything calling `apply_chat_template` (fine-tuning frameworks, eval harnesses) will silently treat the model as chat-capable. **(a)** Ship + card warning: keeps the weight tree untouched, helps humans but not programmatic consumers. **(b)** Strip the template[^strip]: correct capability signaling; costs a re-cut + re-pin + smoke re-test, but *not* new parity numerics — the parity suite feeds explicit token IDs and never uses the template. External review leans (b); weights are identical either way. 3. **No private staging: upload public → verify → announce.** The free-org private-storage cap is 100 GB, under the 125 GiB tree[^storage]. Public storage is free, and the artifact risk is retired pre-upload (hash-pinned, parity-tested, live-tested below). To be candid: the repo is publicly discoverable (org page, feeds) from the moment upload starts, and deletion is a failure response, not a recall — accepted because the artifact is verified before upload begins. 4. **License & data disclosure.** Proposal: `apache-2.0` (marin-8b precedent) — but precedent isn't approval; a release owner should explicitly approve the license for *these weights*, and we ship a `LICENSE` file (plus `NOTICE` if required) alongside the README. The team also needs to supply a one-paragraph training-data description covering the full 2.3T-token lineage (the card currently describes only the 211B cooldown mix) and state decontamination status. [^strip]: Stripping must cover both `chat_template.jinja` and any `chat_template` field embedded in `tokenizer_config.json`. [^storage]: [HF storage limits](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/storage-limits): free org = 100 GB private, public = free; PRO ($9/mo) = 1 TB private. marin-community shows no paid-plan badge, but only an org admin can confirm billing — preflight item below. CoreWeave egress = $0. If the org turns out to have paid private storage, staging privately first is a strictly-nicer variant of the same plan. ## What ships The pinned bf16 export tree `d819cbc63780bd86` — re-cut by #7458 under the single-name config contract (#7447); exactly reproduced from the checkpoint, with Levanter parity and the 64-case vLLM representative set matching the frozen goldens — plus `README.md` and `LICENSE`, which sit outside the hashed tree. | Asset | Details | |---|---| | Weights | 39 safetensors shards, bf16, ~125 GiB; 44-file core-tree digest `tree-sha256 = d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0` (README/LICENSE excluded) | | `config.json` | Single-name contract (#7447 Option A) — verified in the shipped file: one key per field, no aliases | | Tokenizer | `tokenizer.json` (17 MB) + `tokenizer_config.json` — Marin tokenizer, 128,256 vocab | | `chat_template.jinja` | Decision 2 | | `model.safetensors.index.json` | Shard index | | `README.md`, `LICENSE` | Added at upload (outside the hashed tree) | Not shipped: optimizer states / raw Levanter checkpoint (stay internal), `generation_config.json` (absent from the export; vLLM reads EOS/BOS from `config.json`). ## Release steps - [x] Config contract merged, export re-cut (#7447 → #7458; only `config.json` changed, weights byte-identical) - [x] Fork tag **`snowball-v1`** created — a curated pointer the card commands reference; currently at `afb26719464d5957e695bde478ae93a160b11d14` (what `marin.inference.tpu_vllm_pins` pins for serving), advancing as the fork improves. The exact tested revision is recorded in the card's Provenance - [x] Card commands tested end-to-end on 8×H100 (protocol below) - [ ] Team review of this issue (decisions 1–4) + training-data paragraph from decision 4 - [ ] Preflight: name the uploader; org admin confirms billing plan and repo create/write/delete permissions; HF write token on the upload node (never echoed to logs) - [ ] Create public repo, `hf upload-large-folder` the tree from a CoreWeave node, add README + LICENSE - [ ] **Verification gate** (all pass/fail, before any announcement): (1) on a clean HF cache *without credentials*, download the repo; (2) verify the exact 44-file list and core-tree digest, bf16-only tensors, and single-name config; (3) serve the downloaded snapshot with the card command on 8×H100-80GB and reproduce the greedy completion; (4) rerun the 64 representative vLLM parity cases against it; (5) check rendered card, links, and license files. Card fixes happen now, not after. - [ ] Capture the final Hub commit SHA, create a Hub tag (`step-42150`), and record both plus the tested fork SHA in the card's Provenance — announce that revision, not moving `main` - [ ] Announce; housekeeping: close #7447 + #7366, delete the old `781bc329` tree (per #7458), add to the Hero Runs collection Failure response: public availability begins when upload starts; if the gate fails, stop, delete or repair the repo, and assume already-downloaded bytes cannot be recalled. After announcing, released revisions are preserved and fixes land as new commits. ## Model card (full `README.md`)
README.md as it will appear on the Hub ````markdown --- license: apache-2.0 language: - en pipeline_tag: text-generation library_name: vllm tags: - moe - mixture-of-experts - base-model - marin - grug --- # Snowball — Grug 67B-A2B base checkpoint (2.3T training tokens) **Snowball** is a research checkpoint from the [Marin project](https://marin.community): a 67B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model with ~2B active non-embedding parameters per token (Marin's **Grug** architecture), released as a **base model**. It is an *early* checkpoint — an intermediate cooldown taken ~2.3T tokens into a planned 10T-token run — not a final release. > ⚠️ **Stock `transformers`, `vllm`, and `sglang` cannot load this model.** The > architecture (`model_type: grug_moe`) is deliberately not upstreamed yet — it is still > evolving. Use [Marin's vLLM fork](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm) pinned below; > it registers the architecture natively (no `trust_remote_code`). The 8×H100 vLLM > command below is the supported external path; other links are reference implementations. ## Model Sources - **Project page:** [marin.community](https://marin.community) - **Core repo:** [marin-community/marin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin) - **Model definition (JAX/Levanter):** [`experiments/grug/moe/model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/experiments/grug/moe/model.py) · [`lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/lib/levanter/src/levanter/models/snowball.py) - **Training config (this checkpoint's cooldown):** [`moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step39k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_cooldown_step39k_seq64k_bs1024_rep8_muon_10T.py) - **Inference:** [marin-community/vllm](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm) (GPU — supported path) · [marin-community/tpu-inference](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference) (TPU — reference) - **Training run:** [marin#6811](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811) · [W&B logs](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k) ## Quickstart (vLLM fork, 8×H100-80GB) Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and a recent NVIDIA driver — no CUDA toolkit needed with the flags below. ```sh VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \ uvx --from 'vllm @ git+https://github.com/marin-community/vllm.git@snowball-v1' \ vllm serve marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN ``` `snowball-v1` is a curated tag that advances as the fork improves; the exact revision this card was verified against is in [Provenance](#provenance). On the tested node, first launch took ~10 min after weights were local (~4 min one-time `uvx` setup + ~6 min server startup); warm starts ~6 min. The 125 GiB download depends on your network. ```sh curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "marin-community/snowball-67b-a2b-base", "prompt": "The capital of France is", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 32}' ``` Why these flags: 5 KV heads don't divide across 8 GPUs, so the model runs tensor-parallel 1 with its 256 experts sharded across GPUs (~17 GB/GPU). `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` uses prebuilt kernels instead of compiling the fork; `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN` selects the parity-validated backend; the sampler env var avoids a FlashInfer path that JIT-compiles with `nvcc` at startup. ## Architecture | | | |---|---| | Total / active parameters | 67B / ~2B non-embedding active per token | | Hidden size | 2560 | | Layers | 26 — full-attention (NoPE) on every 4th + the last; 2,048-token sliding window (half-RoPE) elsewhere | | Attention | 20 heads / 5 KV heads (GQA), head_dim 128, attention temperature `qk_mult ≈ 1.5703` | | Experts | 256 routed, 4 active per token, expert FFN 1280, shared expert FFN 2560 | | Context | 65,536 positions (served here at 32,768) | | Vocabulary | 128,256 (Marin tokenizer) | Grug combines QB load-balanced sigmoid expert routing, GatedNorm, exclusive self-attention (XSA), and the hybrid sliding/full attention split — which is why stock inference stacks cannot load it. Reference implementations: the pinned vLLM fork and Levanter's `SnowballConfig`. ## Training Snowball was produced by branching at step 39,000 (≈ **2.11T tokens**, ~21% of schedule) of Marin's in-progress 10T-token run ([marin#6811](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6811)) and applying a completed **211B-token** early cooldown (3,150 steps): Datakit phase-1 mix, sequence length switched 8,192 → 65,536, Muon learning rate decayed to the schedule floor, on TPU v4-2048. The checkpoint is complete; the parent 10T run and post-trained variants are outside this release. ## Evaluation Selected comparisons from Marin's six-model eval run ([marin#7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345) — full grid and protocol there). HumanEval used the completions API for every model. | | mmlu | arc-c | hellaswag | winogrande | truthfulqa | boolq | piqa | obqa | gsm8k | humaneval | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | snowball | 0.692 | 0.642 | 0.831 | 0.714 | 0.460 | 0.833 | 0.832 | 0.474 | 0.738 | 0.598 | | qwen3-8b | 0.749 | 0.675 | 0.765 | 0.704 | 0.544 | 0.866 | 0.774 | 0.416 | 0.897 | 0.628 | | llama3.1-8b-instruct | 0.664 | 0.608 | 0.802 | 0.739 | 0.545 | 0.855 | 0.814 | 0.462 | 0.801 | 0.622 | Metrics: acc (mmlu 5-shot, winogrande, boolq); acc_norm (arc-c 25-shot, hellaswag 10-shot, piqa, obqa); mc2 (truthfulqa); exact_match flexible-extract (gsm8k 5-shot); pass@1 (humaneval). ## Limitations - **Base model.** No instruction tuning, no RLHF, no safety training. It continues text; it does not follow instructions or chat. It has not been safety-evaluated and may generate inaccurate, biased, or harmful text; not intended for high-stakes use. - **The bundled chat template is not trained behavior.** It comes from the shared Marin tokenizer. `/v1/chat/completions` will respond, but expect hallucinated extra conversation turns. Use the completions API. - **Weak long-prompt performance.** 7 of 26 layers attend beyond the 2,048-token window, but performance degrades with prompt length; some long-prompt MMLU subjects score near chance ([marin#7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345)). - English-centric training mix. ## Provenance - Checkpoint: step 42,150 of run `moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k-79ebf3` - Export: bf16, 44-file core-tree sha256 `d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0` (README/LICENSE excluded), reproducible via [`tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_hf_bf16_export.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7cb0ae696c65061eb342746d6c7d92d38347f487/tests/cluster/vllm/test_snowball_hf_bf16_export.py) - `config.json` follows the single-name contract of [marin#7447](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7447) - Serving fork verified at commit [`afb26719`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/afb26719464d5957e695bde478ae93a160b11d14) (`snowball-v1` at release time) - Released Hub revision: *(commit + `step-42150` tag recorded here after verification)* Questions and issues: [marin-community/marin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues). ````
## Testing protocol (run 2026-07-21, before filing) Goal: prove the card commands work in an end-user-shaped environment, not our internal harness. **Env:** one 8×H100-80GB node (`cw-us-east-02a` dev pod), NVIDIA driver only — **no CUDA toolkit / `nvcc`** — `uv` as the only Python tooling, weights on local NVMe. 1. Synced the pinned tree from S3 (44 files, ~125 GiB, ~4 min); recomputed the tree hash with the repo's `_tree_sha256` algorithm → **bit-exact match** with `SNOWBALL.export_sha256`. What I served is the parity-tested artifact. 2. Ran the quickstart **verbatim except one substitution**: local weights path in place of the repo id (which doesn't exist until release — the delta the verification gate re-tests). 3. Server up in ~6 min warm (+~4 min first-time uvx setup); engine fingerprint `vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1465+gafb267194-dp8-ep` — the pinned fork revision, DP-8 + expert parallel; ~77 GiB resident/GPU. 4. Greedy completion: `"The capital of France is"` → `" Paris, a city renowned for its cultural and historical significance. The Eiffel Tower, …"`. A separate 256-token request took 2.2 s (~115 tok/s, single stream). 5. Chat probe (decision 2 evidence): `"What is 2+2?"` → `"The answer is 4.\nuser\nWhat is 3+3?\nassistant\n…"` — mechanically fine, semantically a base model. issues.body:
## Goal

Run a weight-merging loop on spare Marin compute: merge Snowball checkpoints on CPU (reserved v4 hosts in us-central2-b), screen the merges cheaply with TPU vLLM on preemptible single-host slices, and promote winners to the H100 policy evaluation. This issue tracks the project end to end.

## Pins

- Marin base `24ce375f06`
- vLLM fork `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d` (head of marin-community/tpu-inference#27, stacked on #29 and #28), applied job-locally
- Evalchemy `3bb8278`, MATH500 full set, harness seed 19311
- S = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` @ `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`

## Status

| Step | State |
|---|---|
| Inventory, feasibility, campaign matrix | done 2026-10-15 |
| Parents S, C, A5, M staged and sha256-verified in `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/rsi-merge/parents/` | done 2026-10-16 |
| Merge toolkit: allowlisted BF16 to F32 widening for M's router biases (branch `task/197`) | done, no PR yet |
| TPU scoring smoke test | done: TPU scores 6-7 points below H100 |
| Matched H100 control | done 2026-10-17: 0.944 |
| Quantized serving on v5e | blocked: the pinned fork rejects every quant config for GrugMoE |
| Localize the TPU gap | in progress (#10250) |
| Iteration-one merges (3 recipes) | not started, waiting on the scoring path |

## MATH500 scores for S, same model revision, same Evalchemy pin, same effective sampling

| Server | Score |
|---|---|
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-03 record | 0.950 |
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-17 | 0.944 |
| TPU v6e-8 TP8 bf16 (two runs) | 0.878, 0.882 |
| TPU v5p-8 TP4 bf16 | 0.884 |

Per item: 421 right everywhere, 39 right on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU, 12 wrong everywhere. The 39 are long solutions; 22 of them drift onto a different problem mid-solution.

## The TPU gap (#10250)

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 items match the H100 within noise up to token 2047 and diverge from exactly token 2048, which is S's `sliding_window` (`global_every` 4). The gap grows to about 0.14 nat mean absolute logprob difference by 3-4k tokens.

Ruled out: truncation, thinking mode, sampling (Evalchemy strips temperature and seed, both servers run vLLM defaults), batch dependence, sharding degree and chip generation (v5p-8 TP4 scores the same), cross-request contamination, mask off-by-one (training, FA3 and the TPU kernel all keep the last W tokens including self), KV block eviction (the TPU runner keeps one full-attention cache group), per-layer window plumbing (reaches the TPU kernel unchanged; global layers get no window), KV cache dtype (bf16 on both).

Not valid controls at this pin: `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` (never read by the vLLM model), a GPU TP8 run (GPU GrugMoE requires TP=1), the experimental batched RPA kernel (fails to compile: its SMEM schedule is sized from a reported capacity above the compiler's 1 MiB limit).

A standalone probe of the pinned ragged-paged-attention v3 kernel against its dense reference with random inputs passes 22 cases around the window boundary (error flat at bf16 noise). Random inputs spread attention over about 2048 keys, so that probe cannot see an edge or sink effect. Running now: a kernel probe with peaky scores, a BOS-like sink key and position-bucket values, and a TPU serving control with the window disabled.

Consequence for the loop: TPU vLLM cannot rank merges until this is fixed. One H100x8 MATH500 run costs about 14 minutes of box time per candidate.

## Related

- #10250 TPU sliding-window divergence
- #9400 tpu-inference pin bump and hardware checks
- #8323 Snowball TPU serving
- #7555 earlier long-context divergence on TPU
- marin-community/tpu-inference#28 custom router selections, #29 host storage release, #27 TP8 head padding (the stack every TPU run here used)
- Two Evalchemy integration gotchas found on the way: the pinned Evalchemy strips `temperature` and `seed` from requests, so the server's defaults apply; and marin's FineStore result reader expects native results JSON while Evalchemy `3bb8278` writes parquet tables, so the parent eval job reports FAILED although the child succeeded and the score is in `data/evalchemy_results/`.

## Open decisions

1. Score iteration-one merges on H100 now, or wait for the TPU fix.
2. Open a PR for the merge-toolkit change on `task/197`.
3. File the Iris autoscaler tier-blocking issue (a v6e-4 group in backoff blocks v6e-8 demand in the same zone).

## Localization update: the TPU/H100 gap is the sliding window, and the TPU side matches training

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 MATH500 prompts (Snowball S, `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02@50fe2f48`), now in five configurations: H100 and TPU v6e-8 each with the model's 2048 sliding window and each with the window disabled (`--hf-overrides '{"sliding_window": 262144}'`), plus an H100 repeat for run-to-run noise. Mean |Δ logprob| per position bin:

| positions | H100 vs TPU, window off on both | H100 vs TPU, window on | H100: window on vs off | TPU: window on vs off | H100 repeat noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.014–0.016 | 0.015–0.017 | 0.013–0.015 | 0.000 | 0.013–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.012 | 0.026 | 0.013 | 0.025 | 0.012 |
| 2112–2303 | 0.012–0.014 | 0.037–0.039 | 0.018–0.024 | 0.038–0.041 | 0.011–0.014 |
| 2304–2431 | 0.011–0.017 | 0.040–0.066 | 0.037–0.084 | 0.058–0.114 | 0.010–0.014 |
| 2432–3071 | 0.014–0.015 | 0.066–0.079 | 0.124–0.186 | 0.143–0.211 | 0.012–0.015 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.021 | 0.142 | 0.703 | 0.700 | 0.013 |
| 4096–8000 | 0.033 | 0.133 | 1.123 | 1.096 | 0.010 |

1. With the window off on both platforms, H100 and TPU agree at every position to within 0.03 nats. The whole divergence is in how the 2048 window is applied.
2. On TPU (tpu-inference `ae387b8`, ragged paged attention v3) the window takes effect at token 2049 on every long item. Three standalone kernel probes (random, peaky/sink, and serving's per-shard head geometry and request classes) put exactly zero attention mass outside the window. This matches levanter's training mask (`splash_attention_mask.LocalMask(window_size=(W-1, None))` AND causal, `lib/levanter/src/levanter/kernels/pallas/splash_attention.py`).
3. On H100 (vLLM fork `01911be`, FlashAttention 3) the window's effect stays at noise until about token 2150, is about half the TPU's around token 2340, and equals the TPU's from about 2460 on. Past 3072 the two effects are the same size, so every local layer is windowed on both platforms; the H100 differs only in the first few hundred tokens past the boundary, i.e. it keeps seeing some early tokens that the exact window drops.
4. Ruled out on the TPU side: the kernel, the batched kernel (does not compile at this pin), KV block eviction (one cache group on TPU), KV dtype, per-layer window plumbing, RoPE, prefill chunk size (knee stays at 2048 with 1536-token chunks).

Open: which code path in the FA3 backend produces the loose boundary (an FA2 run is in flight), and why the looser window scores higher on MATH500 (0.944 H100 vs 0.878–0.884 TPU). Data: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-{h100x8,h100x8-nowindow,h100x8-fa3repeat,v6e8,nowindow-v6e8,chunk1536-v6e8}/`.

## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.
