spillover_issues.title: Agent MoE Experiment: Over-Encoding scaling ladder

spillover_issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
spillover_issues.body:
Our data-mixture optimization capital is **bucket-indexed**. A mixture swarm (RegMix/DSP-style) teaches "weight on bucket #7 → loss", and bucket #7 is nothing but a name: the learned surrogate has no representation of what the bucket *contains*. Any change to the bucket layer therefore strands the evidence:

- **Bucket contents drift**: dedup passes, quality relabels, source refreshes, tokenizer changes to a bucket's data all silently invalidate the coefficients learned for its name — with no signal that they did.
- **Bucketing changes**: merging, splitting, or re-partitioning the corpus (e.g. any datakit reorganization) produces buckets the sweep never named. The entire sweep becomes unusable for the new layout.
- **New data has no coordinates**: "should we add dataset X, and at what weight/schedule?" has no principled answer — the surrogate cannot price a bucket it never saw. Current fallbacks are heuristics (token-proportional share, Olmix-style reuse of old ratios) or paying for a fresh sweep.
- **Sweeps cannot be pooled**: swarms run under different bucket eras (different partitions, different quality splits) share no coordinate system, so their runs cannot serve as one training set even when the underlying corpus overlaps heavily.

The cost is recurring and large: a mixture swarm is O(hundreds) of proxy training runs (qsplit240: ~240 mixtures × 2 scales), and the bucket layer changes far more often than the corpus itself. In practice this means mixture decisions are refreshed on sweep cadence, while data curation moves on relabel/refresh cadence — and every gap between the two is bridged by heuristics.

What a solution needs to provide:

1. **Sweep reuse**: existing swarm runs remain valid evidence under bucket redefinition, re-bucketing, and corpus refresh — ideally under a representation that can be recomputed for old runs after the fact.
2. **New-data pricing**: a new dataset can be evaluated for "does it help, at what weight, in which training phase" at a cost far below a sweep (target: hours of CPU + at most a handful of validation runs), with an honest measure of how far the answer extrapolates beyond observed evidence.
3. **Pooling**: runs from different bucket eras (and, eventually, different swarms) can serve as one accumulating training set, so mixture evidence compounds rather than resets.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 One potential fix, designed and validated: **mixing-via-embeddings** (#6969) — describe every bucket by a token-weighted histogram over a frozen embedding codebook and learn the mixture surrogate over the induced *content distribution* (`h = V·w`) instead of bucket names. Bucket identity is consumed in featurization, so old sweeps re-featurize under any future bucketing (reuse + pooling), and a new dataset is priced from one 20k-doc embedding pass + a CPU refit (new-data pricing), with support/novelty diagnostics quantifying extrapolation.

Validation summary (full detail on #6969 and in `.agents/logbooks/mixing-via-embeddings.md` on `rav/mixing-via-embeddings`): pre-registered retrodictive gates passed on qsplit240 (content→value LODO with shuffled/matched controls @60M; held-out-dose retrodiction @300M, beating weights-based incumbents on 32–34/36 domains), and a live pre-registered test passed — the surrogate priced a never-swept bucket (`dolma_starcoder`), proposed a mixture, and realized **0.9410** uncheatable BPB vs olmix-reuse 0.9495 / token-proportional 0.9759 / the sweep's best-ever run 0.9554 (−0.0145, ~8σ vs measured repeat noise). Cost: one embedding job + minutes of CPU + 3 validation runs. Known limits are quantified there too (within-topic quality invisible to embeddings; histogram-dispersion confound; ~0.03 argmax optimism → LCB proposer is the top follow-up).

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Reference for anyone picking this up: how to map the **Grug-MoE Fisher-DSP sweep** buckets to their underlying data.

**The sweep**: [`marin-community/grug-moe-mix-swarm`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/grug-moe-mix-swarm) — 840 MoE runs (d512, us-central2), each a two-phase mixture over **168 buckets**, with `macro_bpb` + 52 per-task BPBs per run. Weight columns are `{bucket: weight}` dicts keyed by bucket name.

**The data**: datakit store `store_8ac06c74` — 40 lexical clusters × 5 quality tiers = 200 partitions, 10.37T tokens total:
- `gs://marin-us-east5/datakit/store_8ac06c74/` (GCS, us-east5)
- `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/store_8ac06c74/` (CoreWeave mirror)

**Mapping rule** (canonical source: `experiments/grug/moe/launch_datakit_moe_mix.py`):

1. **Direct buckets** — name arithmetic, 0-based: `cNNqQ` → `<store>/cluster=NN/quality=Q`. E.g. `c12q3` → `.../cluster=12/quality=3`. 167 buckets.
2. **`tail`** — a `ConcatDatasetComponent` over exactly the **33 below-threshold partitions** (every partition with < ~100–200M tokens; largest merged = 89M, smallest kept = 212M; separation is clean). The explicit child list is `_TAIL_BUCKETS` in the launcher: whole clusters 0, 4, 7, 9, 39 (all tiers) plus `c10q1–q4` and `c38q1–q4`. Combined: 0.42B tokens (0.004% of the store).
3. This one rule explains all bucket-list irregularities: no `c00/c04/c07/c09/c39` (whole clusters below threshold), and `c10`/`c38` appear with only `q0` (only tier above threshold).

**Format & metadata**:
- Each partition is consumed directly as a levanter cache (`flat_cache=True`, `TextLmDatasetFormat`): `part-NNNNN-of-06301/` shard dirs containing `shard_ledger.json` + `input_ids/` tensorstore arrays. No derived per-bucket caches exist.
- Per-partition `total_tokens` / `total_elements` / `n_shards`: `<store>/.artifact.json` (also records `cluster_view: 40`, quality thresholds `[0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8]`).
- Tokenizer: `marin_tokenizer`. Phase 1 starts at 0.8 of total steps (`_PHASE_1_START_FRACTION`); mixture block size 49,152. The launcher has an `enable_simulated_epoching` flag — check the swarm's launch config before interpreting high-dose runs (per-run max weight reaches 0.95, and bucket sizes span 212M→hundreds of B tokens, so epoching behavior matters for any response modeling).

**To build content features (V columns) for these buckets** with the machinery on `rav/mixing-via-embeddings`: sample per partition from the caches above (`experiments/datakit/mixture_features/build_domain_histograms.py` reads this exact format), and build `tail` as a token-count-weighted sample across its 33 children using the `.artifact.json` counts.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Pre-registration: holdout test protocol for the grug-moe-mix-swarm** (before any model fitting on this data; the 840 runs are treated independently of qsplit240).

- **Split (locked)**: 800 train / 40 test, uniform random `numpy default_rng(seed=0)` over `experiment_index`. Test indices in `holdout_manifest.json`; test labels quarantined in a separate file whose SHA-256 is pinned in the manifest (`68a90838…`); both mirrored to `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/v0/grug/`. Coverage checked on features only: test max-dose distribution matches train (15/40 runs above 0.4).
- **Development rules**: all featurization, variants (raw-weights ridge/LGBM incumbents; content ridge K=1000 in the frozen basis; Hellinger kernel; ± quality-tier features; ± epoch/exposure features; shuffled + matched-random controls), hyperparameters, and model selection use the 800 training runs only, via CV. Primary target: `macro_bpb`.
- **One-shot procedure**: freeze the selected model + declared baselines → write predictions for the 40 from features only → **publish the predictions file's SHA-256 here before opening labels** → open the quarantine once → compute only the pre-registered readout (anything further is labeled exploratory).
- **Readout & pass bar**: R1 predictive power (Spearman on the 40, permutation p < 0.001); R2 beats the bucket-indexed incumbent (paired ΔSpearman ≥ 0 vs best weights baseline, bootstrap CI reported); R3 no selection overfit (test Spearman ≥ train-CV − 0.15); R4 semantics-vs-shape decomposition vs matched-random control (measured, no bar). **PASS = R1 ∧ R2 ∧ R3.**

Full protocol: `test_protocol.md` at the GCS path above (sha256 `ef33dce04d156a37…`).

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Pre-registered AMENDMENT to the grug holdout protocol** (before any label opening; the quarantine file remains unopened; all evidence below is train-only CV).

**Why**: development on the 800 training runs showed the original target (`macro_bpb`) mixes an English factor with a reliable-but-mixture-orthogonal multilingual factor (33 belebele/include tasks; English↔belebele macro Spearman 0.10) over a per-run-varying task set — capping the best model at OOF Spearman 0.303 and breaking R1's power at n=40. The swarm's own registered aggregates likewise drop `macro_bpb` and use strict-common English z-means.

**Amended target** (exact formula, replaces macro_bpb): `zmacro_english_20` — for run r, y(r) = mean over observed t ∈ L of (bpb_t(r) − μ_t)/σ_t, where L = the 20 bpb tasks not matching `belebele_*`/`include_*`, and (μ_t, σ_t) are frozen train-set constants recorded in `target_candidates.json` (GCS: `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/v0/grug/`). Lower better. Leak checks: fully-nested selection reproduces the same task list; nested vs frozen z-stats differ by 0.0002 Spearman; PC2 of the task matrix (unsupervised) recovers the same factor at 0.841.

**Selected primary model** (train-CV, frozen): Hellinger-kernel ridge, K=1000 per-phase content histograms, hyperparameters by inner CV — **train-CV OOF Spearman 0.818 ± 0.001** (≈93% of the split-half reliability bound 0.88). Declared baselines frozen alongside: train-mean, weights-ridge (0.679), weights-LGBM, DSP dose-response (best tied variant 0.643 — the qsplit240 functional form does not transfer to this 168-bucket swarm), and the primary's shuffled-columns + matched-random controls.

**Amended readout** (unchanged in structure; R1's bar now properly powered): R1 Spearman(pred, realized) on the 40, permutation p < 0.001; R2 paired ΔSpearman ≥ 0 vs the best weights baseline (bootstrap CI reported); R3 test Spearman ≥ train-CV − 0.15 (i.e. ≥ 0.668); R4 semantic-vs-matched-random decomposition (measured, no bar). PASS = R1 ∧ R2 ∧ R3. Procedure unchanged: predictions for the 40 are generated from features only, their file's SHA-256 gets published here BEFORE the quarantine is opened, labels are opened once, and only the pre-registered readout is computed (rest labeled exploratory).

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body: 🤖 **Holdout test — predictions frozen (phase 1 of the one-shot procedure).** `test_predictions.parquet` SHA-256: `0a4cc4e6430d92001e65b9ecf00873dd02b5666fb29da41c38d77d7d34c2474f` (1040 rows = 26 models × 40 runs; frozen primary Hellinger-kernel γ=1.2475/α=0.1 + declared baselines/controls; embedded provenance: git `ed7599e51a`, target formula + frozen z-stats; mirrored to `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/v0/grug/` with `frozen_model_hyperparams.json` sha `080a504c…`). Quarantined labels accessed by checksum only so far (matches the split manifest). Opening the label file next; only the amended pre-registered readout (R1–R4) will be computed on it.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Grug holdout test — pre-registered verdict: PASS (R1 ∧ R2 ∧ R3).** Quarantine opened exactly once, after hash verification against the published predictions SHA (`0a4cc4e6…`) and the split manifest (`68a90838…`).

| gate | result | numbers |
|---|---|---|
| R1 predictive power | **PASS** | test Spearman **0.7205**, 10k-permutation p = 1e-4 (resolution floor; max permuted ρ 0.588) |
| R2 vs bucket-indexed incumbent | **PASS** | Δ = **+0.035** vs weights-LGBM (0.6852; best baseline), paired 95% CI [−0.14, +0.21] (CI exclusion was pre-declared stretch, not required); vs weights-ridge Δ = +0.089; ΔRMSE −0.037 |
| R3 no selection overfit | **PASS** | 0.7205 ≥ 0.668 bar (train-CV 0.818 − 0.15); generalization gap −0.098 |
| R4 semantics vs shape (measured) | small | Δ vs matched-random control +0.015, 95% CI [−0.05, +0.10]; shuffled control mean-of-10 reaches 0.7212 |

**Honest headline**: the content-featurized surrogate transfers to unseen mixtures (best single model on Spearman and per-seed comparisons, 10/10 vs matched-control seeds) and beats the RegMix-style incumbent — but on this swarm most of the predictive signal is carried by histogram *shape* statistics rather than cross-bucket semantic identity (the R4 margin is CI-consistent with zero at n=40; the `_mean10` controls also enjoy an implicit 10-predictor ensembling advantage). This echoes and strengthens the qsplit240 dispersion-confound finding: for *this* store's cluster×quality buckets, "describedness" earns its keep mostly through shape+geometry, with semantics contributing a small increment.

Campaign summary on this swarm (840 runs, all development on 800 train, one-shot test on 40): target repaired from `macro_bpb` (kernel OOF 0.303 — capped by a mixture-orthogonal multilingual factor) to the pre-registered `zmacro_english_20` (0.818 train-CV, ≈93% of the split-half reliability bound); DSP functional form ported and retired for this regime (best tied variant 0.643; content-tied parameterization was its best flavor on both targets); Hellinger-kernel K=1000 per-phase selected and confirmed. Artifacts: `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/v0/grug/` (`holdout_readout.{json,md}`, `realized_vs_predicted.parquet`, full CV/DSP/target reports); code on `rav/mixing-via-embeddings`.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body: 🤖 Addendum refining the earlier "epoch features inert" finding (train-CV only, post-holdout, exploratory relative to the completed test): on the clean `zmacro_english_20` target, hinge exposure features give the **linear** content model a solid gain (hist-ridge 0.740 → 0.770, +0.030, 15/15 folds, p=1e-4) — `macro_bpb`'s multilingual noise had masked the repetition signal. The **kernel** does not benefit: a product hell×hinge kernel scores 0.767 vs 0.815 alone (−0.047, 0/15) — it already absorbs epoching implicitly through content-dose geometry, and explicit terms dilute its distance structure (same failure mode as kernel+quality). The frozen holdout primary stands; epoch caps at proposal time remain mandatory either way.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Independent validation pass (Codex-collaborative): rigor vs PR #2393, epoching audit, literature review.** Two adversarial Codex CLI review rounds; its three prescribed analyses executed; corrections adopted. Full memo + artifacts: `validation_memo.md`, `codex_methodology_review.md`, `validation_checks.md`, `epoching_lit_review.md` at `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/v0/grug/`.

**Rigor vs #2393**: exceeds on pre-registration (SHA commitment chain, quarantined holdout, amend-before-open), semantic controls (shuffled/matched-random — absent in #2393), and heterogeneous replication (two swarms + one live training test); falls short on seed-repeat noise panels, heteroskedasticity analysis, and metric-registry formality. Top data ask: a ~10-run grug seed-repeat panel (would settle the noise ceiling, bracketed at 0.837–0.923 by residual decomposition; achieved 0.8147 ≈ 97% of the pessimistic bound).

**Epoching: validated with two corrections.** Computation confirmed correct (target-budget semantics, 0.767/0.233 phase quantization). The monotone discount has the same effective-data functional form as Muennighoff 2023 (fitted δ=0.10 ⇒ R_D\*≈9 vs literature 15–31); simulated epoching at proxy scale matches what the [2026 repetition-mismatch work recommends](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07597); keep-caps-regardless is the published recommendation. Corrections: (1) the earlier "kernel absorbs epoching" was partly an artifact of a bad product-kernel construction — **concat-ARD beats the plain kernel** (+0.0049, 12/15 folds, p=0.0015; linear models gain 6× more), so the kernel absorbs *most* of it and concat-ARD is the refit upgrade; (2) hinge knots move {1,4,8}→{1,4,16} (16 ≈ fitted half-life). Cap per phase, explicitly: `w_j ≤ 4·T_j/(f_p·target_budget)`.

**Selection integrity**: replicated-selection bootstrap (B=200) finds no selection optimism (−0.011 ± 0.002, negative); the realized holdout 0.7205 sits 1.3–1.6 SE below the de-biased train expectation (P ≈ 0.08 under sampling noise — consistent, not established; hyperparams frozen in the bootstrap, so the check is approximate). The campaign's formula-fixed target choice was more conservative than the replicated argmax rule.

**Corrected-claims register** (in the memo): semantic value is validated on qsplit240 only (grug validates *prediction*; controls match the primary there); "no replicates needed" (H3) → "not cost-effective at ~8σ on borrowed noise"; monotone discount is a literature-consistent prior, not a validated conclusion in this sweep.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 **Validation campaign checkpoint: codex-collaborative loop reached its terminal state.** Four adversarial Codex CLI rounds; all its prescribed analyses executed. Round-4 verdict: *"Nothing material remains validatable without new data … rigorously bounded rather than overclaimed."*

New since the last update: **budget correction** — the 840 grug runs each trained **100.16B tokens** (verified from executor_info; not 525M as previously derived) → corrected phase fractions propagated through all epoch-sensitive analyses (all findings survive: hinge +0.0269, concat-ARD +0.0038); **robustness batch** — calibration near-affine (slope 1.020; tail rank weakness = range restriction), LODO-by-cluster median 0.682 vs 0.853 control (interpolation-dependence quantified, worst clusters named), top-1 mixture recommendation unstable (42%) vs cluster-level robust (Jaccard 0.76–0.93) → **recommend at cluster granularity**, negative control clean, heteroskedasticity clean, and the first fitted per-group repetition half-lives (code-adjacent R_D\*≈9 vs web ≈1.9; no OOF gain, informative constants). **Deliverables**: a fully self-contained HTML report (figures + four-tier claim table separating validated@100B-seed0 / unvalidated-across-seeds / unvalidated-across-budgets / not-supported) at `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/v0/report/`, with a verification log covering 19 skeptic findings + coordinator's support-honesty fix to the dose-response demo. **In flight**: the 10-run seed-repeat panel at the exact verified swarm config (rav-approved, ~1,110 v4-8-hours; children pending us-central2 autoscale) — resolves tier B (seed variance) in ~5 days.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 form-selection campaign settled — latest results

decision-focused write-up (7 figures, one per decision, each with a collapsible "what am I looking at?" explainer): https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/mixing-via-embeddings/2026.07.21.1/index.html

**model**: `ŷ(w,B,d) = kernel(h = V·w) + Σⱼ bⱼ·max(eⱼ − τⱼ, 0)` — a bucket-independent content surrogate (Hellinger-kernel ridge over per-phase embedding histograms) + a linear-past-threshold epoch-harm term. new source = new column of `V` → priced without re-sweeping.

* **surrogate = kernel** — held-out Spearman **0.720** on the 40-run quarantined test set (p<1e-4, perm-max 0.588), ~79% of the seed-noise ceiling; beats weights-ridge / lgbm / RFF / KME / NN in the bake-off. in-regime it misses no repetition harm (0/37 tasks)
* **epoch-harm form = linear-past-threshold** — leave-one-epoch-out CV-decisive: code CV-RMSE 0.056 bpb vs quadratic 0.246 / softplus² 0.260 (curved forms over-extrapolate e32 by 10–30σ). the committed swoosh was wrong in magnitude (~119×), shape, and onset
  * threshold is **per-bucket**: τ_code≈8.85, τ_math≈11.66 (CI95 [9.9, 13.3] excludes 8.85) → needs per-bucket calibration
  * amplitude per content-type + scale-aware: `bⱼ = b₀·(B/10B)^−0.73·(d/512)^1.68`; per-epoch damage math (0.091) > code (0.052) > web (0.014)
  * generalizes across 3 independent bucket types (code / math / web)
* **★ 100B production gate — harm VANISHES** — matched-mechanism run (real `max_train_batches` subset-repeat, same mechanism as the 10B harm experiments, so only budget changed): e4→e16 rise = **−0.003 bpb** (0.4σ from zero, 9.3σ below the power-law prediction). 4-point budget-transfer curve harm(e16) {2.5,10,40,100}B = {0.688, 0.384, 0.092, −0.003}, fitted exponent **−1.15** (steeper than the −0.73 mid-range → collapses faster than the power law). agrees with the transect under a matched mechanism
  * → **at production scale (100B) the kernel alone suffices**; the harm term is a proxy-scale / extreme-repetition (≥~16–32 epoch) guardrail, not a core production requirement. the severe 10B harm (e16 +0.39, e32 +1.27 bpb) was a small-budget artifact
  * caveat: single-seed per point; a small +8.8σ residual (+0.07 bpb) survives only at e32 (extreme over-repetition), ~3.4× weaker than the 10B fit

**test-set protocol** was pre-registered before any look; the 40-run quarantine held throughout.[^1]

[^1]: remaining roadmap (refinements, not blockers): web-shape densification at 10B, combined-model held-out validation against the sacred set, codebook (K) sensitivity. artifacts under `gs://marin-eu-west4/user/rav/projects/mixing_via_embeddings/`.

spillover_issues.body:
# Requirements  
1. For a given checkpoint, run our complete list of evals (or a specified subset) on it
2. Publish the results on the eval leaderboard (from a single-source-of-truth database) (tracked here: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6043) 
3. This should work for our own models and others (see https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4827) 
4. There should be a defined path (and agent skill) for adding more evals + the set of evals should be visible on the leaderboard

This should work for our own models and others that we support inference on (e.g. on vLLM). 

# Definition of done
New checkpoint trigger (TBD below how) → configured eval subset runs via the OpenAI-HTTP contract (#4827) → results land in the DB → appear on the leaderboard (#6043), with zero manual steps.

# Decisions to make
- **TPU vs GPU, or both** Should we start with TPUs, or focus on having this run on GPUs? (Do we need to make this decision?) Our default path is both (#6041 and #6042).
- **Trigger definition**: Do we want this to run on all model checkpoints as they land (where?) How do we want the system to determine which specific checkpoints to automatically run on?


# Related issues
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5887
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6041
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6042
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5005

## Specific evals
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6703 — Marin AA-II validation suite
- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6360


- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7638 — RULER long-context eval through the evalchemy fork

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
**Claude finished @ihodes's task in 1m 18s** —— [View job](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/29769915281)

---
### What #7405 delivered vs. what remains in #6503

#7405 (merged, closed #7345) built the **eval execution + reporting engine**. Mapping it against this issue's requirements:

| # | Requirement | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run full eval list (or subset) for a checkpoint | ✅ Done | `experiments/evaluation/cli.py launch --model X --evals core\|smoke\|<subset>`. `core` = 11 lm-eval/evalchemy tasks; one serve, N evals, N durable records. |
| 2 | Publish to leaderboard from a SSOT DB (#6043) | 🟡 Partial | Records (`record.json`) are the SSOT; `infra/evaldash/` (Cloud Run + CloudSQL Postgres index, evaldash.oa.dev) renders the model × eval grid. But this is the *eval dashboard*, not yet reconciled with the public leaderboard tracked in #6043. |
| 3 | Works for our models **and** others via vLLM/OpenAI-HTTP (#4827) | ✅ Done | Demonstrated on snowball + 5 HF models; serves over the OpenAI-compatible contract; TPU (v5e→v6e→v5p sizing) and GPU (CoreWeave). |
| 4 | Defined path + **agent skill** for adding evals; evals visible on leaderboard | 🟡 Partial | README "Adding a model or eval" documents the path (`EvalSuiteConfig`→`EVALS`, `EvalModelConfig`→`MODELS`); evals are visible as dashboard columns. **No agent skill exists** (only `evaluate-zephyr-perf`, unrelated). |

### Remaining work

**1. Automated checkpoint trigger — the core gap (blocks the Definition of Done).**
The DoD is *"New checkpoint trigger → eval subset runs → results in DB → leaderboard, with zero manual steps."* #7405 provides only **manual** entry points: the `launch` CLI and a `pipeline.py` `eval_step` `ArtifactStep`. There is no code that watches for new checkpoints and auto-launches evals — no watcher/webhook/poller in `experiments/evaluation/`. This is the "Automated" in "Automated eval system" and is still entirely open. It also subsumes the open **"Trigger definition"** decision in the issue: *which* checkpoints auto-run, and *where* the trigger lives (checkpoint-export step hook, GCS-landing poll, WandB/registry event, cron sweep, etc.). The `eval_step` ArtifactStep is the natural building block — remaining work is wiring it to fire automatically.

**2. Leaderboard reconciliation (#6043).**
Evaldash exists and reads the SSOT records, but the issue asks for results on *the leaderboard* (#6043). Need to confirm whether evaldash **is** that leaderboard or whether records/DB still need to feed the #6043 surface. Likely a scope/ownership question rather than net-new plumbing.

**3. Agent skill for adding evals (requirement #4).**
Requirement #4 explicitly asks for a defined path **and an agent skill**. The README path exists; the skill does not. A `.agents/skills/add-eval/` playbook (mirroring `add-dataset`) would close this.

**4. Decision now resolved by #7405: TPU vs GPU.**
The issue flagged "TPU vs GPU, or both" as undecided — #7405 does **both** (TPU sizing heuristic + CoreWeave GPU shapes), so this decision can be marked resolved.

### Summary
#7405 nails requirements **1** and **3** and most of **2/4** (execution, multi-backend serving, durable SSOT records, a dashboard, a documented add-eval path). What remains for "Automated eval system" to be done:
- **the automatic checkpoint trigger** (biggest item; also resolves the open "Trigger definition" decision),
- **reconcile evaldash with the #6043 leaderboard**, and
- **add the `add-eval` agent skill**.

This matches @rjpower's "partly fixed in #7405" — the manual pipeline is there; the automation and leaderboard-integration layers are not yet.

Ben's Definition of Done (must-have)

1. A firm list of evals we will prioritize in 2026 (agentic, non agentic) that are in-distribution (Hill climbable)
2. An approved Marin eval policy; under what set of shared hparams do we eval
3. A preliminary list of baselines we will commit to maintain (comparable models, experimental models we care about for post)
4. Successful e2e parity tests for all approved baselines on all approved evals under the approved policy; a parity test here means we are no more than 1-2 stdev from a published result from a venue we trust
5. Nightly spot check parity testing to ensure no regression
6. A plan to integrate all evals that are high priority and by-whens and DRIs (e.g., AAII proxy evals)
7. Documentation on how to self-eval a model
8. A clean, well documented way to modify all model serving params at runtime
9. The ability to run arbitrary custom evals by passing in Harbor and Evalchemy and vLLM configs, with reasonable expectations of self-service ... e.g., do some due diligence before raising an issue on parity for an unsupported model or eval
11. A documented path for adding new models or evals
12. A live dashboard with filters that shows scores, stderr, date eval ran, codebase versions, model version, base model for RL / SFT if any, highlights incomplete evals and infra errors, links to model traces, verifier outputs, and other relevant artifacts, serving hardware, serving params
13. Automatic resuming of evals with errors
14. The ability to self-resume evals with model errors
15. Expectation of immutability; evals cannot accidentally disappear or be clobbered or be mutated after capture without a clear logging of the change

spillover_issues.author: hammer
spillover_issues.body: [MeCo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.01956) looks like a promising approach to improve data efficiency in pretraining. We should evaluate it.

comments.author: hammer
comments.body:
Others have evaluated and extended this approach!
- [When Does Metadata Conditioning (NOT) Work for Language Model Pre-Training?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.17562) has some negative results
- [URLs Help, Topics Guide](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16570) and [Beyond URLs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.21613) has many useful analyses of extensions. Their "fine-grained beats coarse-grained" finding is important. I also think that examining whether uniform interleaving of prepended/non-prepended documents is preferred to MeCo's 90% prepended followed by 10% non-prepended "cooldown" schedule is worth investigating.
- [KoCo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12397) prepends 3 dimensions related to source, content, and stability. The Beyond Urls paper found that multiple metadata channels made learning faster early but eventually converged. It's probably worth testing the claims in this paper that they've found a way to make multiple metadata channels have durable value.

There's a lot of potential interaction with the data classification, selection, and mixing work to think about too, e.g. https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/3049 and https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2403. There's some commentary on this interaction in [Topic Over Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16802) and [WebOrganizer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10341). MeCo tested their approach on top of DCLM-fasttext-filtered data and showed the gains stack, but it's not clear if they'd wash out with topics and mixing.

There's also a lot of related work that adds metadata to documents but is less focused on pretraining data efficiency
- [CTRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05858): control codes to constrain generation to a particular style. There is a [#style-tokens](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1409936157822681110) channel in the Marin Discord on this topic that is currently inactive.
- [PHF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.08582): adds reward-model derived preference scores as control tokens for toxicity, PII, and code style.
- [IML](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15047): shows that models may learn source reliability implicitly.
- [Source-Aware Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01019): appends document identifiers for attribution. 
- [Physics of Language Models: Part 3.3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05405): Result 12 talks about prepending special tokens.
- [On the Power of Context-Enhanced Learning in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01821): coins "context-enhanced learning" for the general approach of adding content to documents that does not impact gradient updates. The paper mostly considers the post-training setting though.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
**Symptom.** Generation jobs in cw-us-east-02a each serve an OpenAI-compatible proxy as an Iris link endpoint (`/glm-harbor/<run>-<id>`). Agents call it through its capability URL (`https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/t/...`) once per agent step. On 2026-10-20 at about 04:50Z, a `GET /v1/models` on such an endpoint took 6–10 s through the capability URL. The same request sent directly to the endpoint's registered address from inside its container took under 10 ms. At the same time, capability URLs for endpoints in cw-rno2a (vLLM servers) answered the same request in 0.15–0.5 s from the same client. About 900 concurrent agent trials sat behind cw-us-east-02a endpoints then: 28 jobs × 32 trials, 56 registered endpoints. That was roughly double the load before about 03:10Z.

**Measurements**

| | result |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` via capability URL, cw-us-east-02a endpoint (4 endpoints, 3–6 calls each) | 5.9–10.5 s; connect 0.01 s; nearly all of it is time to first byte |
| same endpoint, direct to its registered address from its own container | 0.000–0.009 s |
| `GET /v1/models` via capability URL, cw-rno2a endpoint, same client, same minute | 0.15–0.49 s |
| per agent step, gap from model reply to the next request (job request logs) | p50 0.4–1.3 s before ~03:05Z; 23–28 s after ~03:40Z |
| model backend latency per request, measured at the proxy (same window) | unchanged: p50 0.8 → 1.0 s, 6.7 → 6.9 ms per output token |

**Ruled out**
- The proxy process: it answers directly in under 10 ms, uses 5–7% of a core, and the containers have no CPU limit.
- The model backend: its latency and per-token speed are unchanged.
- The sandboxes (Daytona): command execution takes 20–80 ms per call, CPU speed is normal, host load is 22–37 on 64 cores.
- Client-side connection setup: connect time is 0.01 s, and the delay is all time to first byte.

**Not available.** There are no gateway or endpoint-relay metrics from before the slowdown. Load dependence is inferred from timing: the gap rose from about 03:10Z and leveled off by 03:40Z, as about 450 more trials started behind cw-us-east-02a endpoints. It has not been measured directly.

**Ask**
1. Gateway and endpoint-relay metrics for cw-us-east-02a from 2026-10-20 00:00Z onward: request rate, latency, queue depth and in-flight connections, compared with cw-rno2a.
2. Is there a per-cluster limit on proxied endpoint traffic (connection pool, worker count, a single relay stream to the cluster) that about 900 concurrent clients would saturate? If so, can it be raised, or should high-request-rate clients use another path?

spillover_issues.body:
Draft here for the v0 part: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xwrIz-HSw_fI7HXqCtVxTi5PXiMrFOPpvd_4B8hm6LM/edit?usp=sharing 

----

Write a shareable design for fast-turnaround Snowball RL curriculum construction, covering the initial training pool and the quality/annotation pilot.

Deliver the draft in `docs/design/snowball-rl-curriculum.md` and publish its reviewable text here. Keep proposed behavior, locally implemented behavior, and executed data/model results distinct.

Done when:

- [x] Specify the v0 target, Ben-derived source recipe, explicit expansion policy, source/difficulty sampling, and handling of insufficient unique environments.
- [x] Pin the converted corpus and admitted catalog; define task identity, holdout grouping, evaluation exclusion, private verifier boundaries, and artifact provenance.
- [ ] Specify the fixed 10k pilot: source-stratified selection, decision-model quality filtering, DeepSeek Flash summaries/tags/difficulty, and Harrier summary embeddings.
- [ ] Define how source, difficulty, semantic diversity, and measured online learning feedback affect later sampling.
- [ ] Name acceptance checks and the current-stack integration gate; separate static quality opinions from executed verifier and rollout evidence.
- [ ] Record unresolved source expansion, storage access, bindings, and runtime compatibility decisions.
- [ ] Complete an independent cold-reader review and link the implementation issues.

The [existing capability catalog and embedding workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curriculum/README.md) supply reusable inputs. [Ben's v0.1 report](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10305) establishes the historical recipe and its limits; it does not establish a ready 100k pool or calibrated task difficulty.

Related efforts: [#10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314), [#10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315).

Draft complete; team review remains open. The local Markdown draft is reproduced below for sharing.

---

# Snowball RL curriculum: v0 pool and curation pilot

Status: design with v0.2 independently verified and published, 2026-10-19.
Audience: Marin RL and data teams.

Tracking: [v0 pool #10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314),
[10k pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), and
[design review #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Build two artifacts in parallel: a training pool targeting 100,000 distinct tasks
for a fast Snowball RL iteration, and a fixed 10,000-task diagnostic sample for
developing quality review, semantic annotations, and curriculum sampling. Start
v0 from Ben's Snowball source families. Use the pilot to decide how to expand and
reweight them. The approved v0.2 pool contains 100,000 independently verified
task contracts and is published in object storage. The private browser has
loaded all 100,000 records. The 10,000-task quality/annotation pilot remains a separate effort;
it is not a requested 10,000-task training subset.

Here, an environment means one task instance with its public interaction
contract and private grader contract. Canonical tasks use TaskSpec; historical
native structural imports retain their original contract. It does not mean a
distinct sandbox image or a generated rollout.

## Inputs and evidence

The [RL Data Atlas](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/)
publication contains 4,998,910 converted task instances: 4,997,251 training
instances across 142 sources, and 1,659 evaluation instances. These are conversion
counts before curation admission or this proposal's duplicate and holdout checks.

| Input | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Converted publication | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-semantics/publication-008e95e5/2026.10.15.1/release.json` |
| Reviewed production catalog | `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production` |
| Native structural pool | [Historical data, revision `cb728a7`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3) |
| Native tokenizer | [Snowball step14, revision `6783e97`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14/tree/6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0) |
| Ben's release evidence | [Snowball v0.1 report, #10305](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10305) |
| Historical mixture | [Pinned `mixture-v2.json`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fed5a9383b92acacbe264c7e601e93d8437218d3/experiments/post_training/smartie/mixture-v2.json) |

Follow each publication source's `curation_root` to converted TaskSpec Parquet.
Resolve the production catalog's per-source artifacts to `final/part-*.parquet`
for admitted rows. Freeze resolved artifact identities and manifest hashes;
`production` is a mutable catalog pointer. Record whether each selected task
appears in both populations and retain the existing admission decision.
The native structural pool is separate from this publication. Its reviewed
import is not production curation admission. Preserve that distinction in
selection provenance and runtime readiness.

Ben's exact historical release has 69,487 training tasks, including 57,364
structural tasks. Its four NVIDIA components contribute 13,023 converted
instances in the larger publication. Thus the 100,000-task target requires an
explicit extension of his source selection. His release supplies no calibrated
task difficulty labels. The pinned mixture expresses intended relative weights
of 0.5 for each NVIDIA family and 1.0 for structural compliance, normalizing to
one sixth each and one third. Historical runtime `weights: {}` and
`shuffle: false` did not establish that exposure ratio: the exported training
population was 82.6% structural. The historical training export also needs
validation against the latest RolloutEngine API; the native API port tracked in
[#10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) is a dependency.

## Effort 1: v0 training pool

### Selection

1. Freeze input snapshots, current runtime revision, selection seed, and source
   allowlist. Preserve Ben's calendar, competitive coding, Reasoning Gym, STEM,
   and structural-compliance families. Enumerate every extension by source ID
   and its family in the selection configuration; exclude unlisted sources.
2. Select admitted canonical training tasks and explicitly reviewed native
   imports, retaining their separate admission status. Exclude evaluation
   sources, declared holdouts, and known benchmark overlaps. Record the matching rule and its
   coverage; a train label alone does not establish absence of contamination.
3. Group exact task contracts using the existing TaskCompendium identity
   machinery. Keep one deterministic representative and retain all source
   aliases. Distinct private grader contracts must remain distinct. Repeated
   public text can share model inference without collapsing task identity.
4. Allocate 100,000 slots without replacement. The approved v0.2 policy starts
   with equal mass across the five families, targeting 20,000 tasks each.
   Within an expanded family, allocate proportional to the square root of eligible source counts.
   Cap sources at availability and redistribute within their family first. If a
   whole family is exhausted, redistribute its remaining slots across families
   with capacity in proportion to their original weights. Record the resulting
   family shares.
5. Within each source, cover available difficulty strata. Use native difficulty
   or generator settings first; otherwise use a versioned manual source/family
   prior with `easy`, `medium`, `hard`, or `unknown` and its rationale. Allocate
   equally across nonempty strata initially, capping and redistributing within
   the same source. Preserve `unknown` as a stratum.
6. Select tasks deterministically from stable identities, shuffle exposure, and
   export TaskSpecs plus selection sidecars. Record requested and actual counts
   by family, source, and difficulty. Report any shortfall without duplicates.

These labels are sampling priors. A long prompt, expensive grader, or low judge
quality score does not by itself establish learning difficulty. V0 fixes the
pool and its initial sampling weights; it does not impose an easy-to-hard
training schedule.

### Current v0.2 materialization

Calendar has 9,115 available tasks. Redistributing its shortfall across the other
four families gives the following allocation:

| Family | Selected contracts |
| --- | ---: |
| Calendar | 9,115 |
| Competitive coding | 22,722 |
| Reasoning Gym | 22,721 |
| STEM | 22,721 |
| Structural compliance | 22,721 |
| Total | 100,000 |

The pool retains all 11,087 admitted canonical structural tasks and adds 11,634
historical native closure tasks. Thus 88,366 selected contracts come from 12
admitted canonical sources, and 11,634 from one reviewed native-import source.
The 244,938-task admitted candidate pool excludes the native input population.
The native pool contains 57,364 records, with 52 duplicate full contracts,
leaving 57,312 eligible contracts and no exact known holdout overlap. Together
the distinct candidate pools contain 302,250 contracts. Exact overlap checks do
not establish semantic decontamination.

Native selection balances eight structural families, then controls within each
family. The import retains byte-exact payloads, native runtime configuration,
and token prefixes under the pinned tokenizer. Full private contracts remain
distinct even when public prompts share cached inference. These native records
retain their historical payloads. A separate adapter now converts the 11,634 selected
native records into current token-preserving TaskSpecs and rollout specifications,
retaining their original identities and private contracts. All selected native tasks
passed reference/invalid scripted completions through the current CPU engine
(23,268 attempts); the other 88,366 task identities remain unchanged.

Published artifact: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/2026.10.19.2`.
Independent verification reconciled payloads and counts, and the
[private browser, revision 2](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/e2bd5c9d-0f93-4ce9-b7af-3c78ca55e5d1/v/2/)
has loaded all 100,000 records. The derived native export passes the current trainer
dataset and scripted worker checks across all eight native families. Updated runtime
packages and trainer pins still need publication, and actual model inference has not
run. Canonical external grader dependencies also need runtime validation. Publication
and CPU checks do not establish full-pool training readiness.

### Release gate

Load the exported pool through the latest RL stack. Exercise roughly 100 distinct
tasks, covering every selected execution/grader contract, with additional cases
if 100 cannot cover them. Check reset, public observation, action handling,
termination, grader invocation, reward interpretation, and resource access.
Retain traces and failures. Quarantine unsupported contracts and regenerate the
allocation before calling the pool runnable. A successful contract smoke does
not establish model quality or training benefit.

## Effort 2: fixed 10,000-task curation pilot

Sample converted training tasks before curation admission so the pilot can
compare existing admission with the proposed filter. Apply evaluation/holdout
exclusion and exact contract grouping first. Keep runtime compatibility as a
separate diagnostic field so unsupported contracts remain visible.

For each source with eligible count \(N_s\), allocate half the sample equally
across sources and half proportional to \(\sqrt{N_s}\). Cap small sources,
redistribute, and round by largest remainder with source-ID tie breaking.
Select deterministically and record inclusion probabilities. The initial
count-only allocation covers 142 sources with 40–480 tasks each; recompute it
after eligibility checks. Freeze the resulting 10,000 input identities and do
not refill rejected tasks. Report every stage against that fixed denominator.

### Processing stages

1. **Quality decision.** Produce `keep`, `reject`, or `uncertain`, reason
   codes, and evidence. Review missing context, inconsistent references,
   answer leakage, ambiguous requirements, and agreement between task and
   verifier. Inspect bounded private grading evidence only in the authorized
   review packet. Preserve existing mechanical/resource checks and executed
   grader controls; model judgment does not replace admission.
2. **DeepSeek Flash annotation.** For kept tasks, generate a 15–40-word
   operational summary, domain/skill tags, interaction mode, and provisional
   difficulty with rationale and confidence. Describe the required knowledge
   and operation. Inputs contain public instructions and public answer/tool
   contracts; exclude solutions, private references, and verifier resources.
3. **Harrier summary embeddings.** Reuse the existing [curation embedding
   pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curation/README.md#task-and-curriculum-embeddings),
   pinned checkpoint, retrieval instruction, pooling, normalization, and
   FineStore caches. Key annotations by full request/model revision and vectors
   by rendered text plus embedding specification. Keep task identity separate
   from public-content identity. Preserve curriculum matching as a diagnostic.
4. **Curriculum sampling.** Cluster summary vectors, then inspect source ×
   difficulty × semantic-cluster coverage. Use cluster coverage to propose v1
   quotas and reduce repeated operations within large sources. Embedding
   similarity alone is neither a rejection rule nor a difficulty measurement.

The decision-model and DeepSeek Flash service IDs, immutable revisions,
request limits, and output schemas must be pinned before inference. They remain
unverified. Measure tokens, latency, failures, and cost on a small initial batch
before processing the full pilot. Persist successful requests and bounded retry
outcomes; retain unresolved failures as explicit rows.

### Pilot evaluation

Audit examples stratified by source and `keep`/`reject`/`uncertain`, with a panel
size set before reviewing outputs. Record human disagreement and concrete error
types. Report quality outcomes, existing-admission disagreement, annotation
coverage, runtime compatibility, and cluster coverage by source. Keep excluded,
failed, and unresolved counts visible.

Run repeated attempts on a roughly 100-task Snowball panel covering source and
provisional difficulty. Use measured success rates and execution cost to check
the priors. This panel supports coarse calibration; it cannot calibrate every
source or establish training improvement. Training comparisons need the same
held-out evaluation protocol and budget.
Before execution, pin the Snowball checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime revision,
attempt count, decoding settings, token/turn/time limits, and pass definition.
Separate infrastructure failures from model failures and retain per-attempt
results against that frozen protocol.

## Artifacts and rollout

Each release retains an immutable input manifest, source/family allowlist,
eligibility and duplicate audits, quotas, selected TaskSpecs, annotation
sidecars, model/prompt revisions, and aggregate reports. Join records on source,
task identity, source locator, and contract digest; avoid lossy joins on task ID
alone. Keep private reviewer packets and credentials out of shared summaries
and team-facing reports. Large task/vector payloads stay in object storage.

| Phase | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- |
| V0 selection | Reconciled counts, exact allowlist, held-out exclusions, reproducible selection |
| V0 runtime gate | Latest-stack contract smoke and documented quarantines |
| Pilot freeze | Exactly 10,000 distinct eligible input identities, or explicit availability shortfall |
| Pilot inference | Pinned service bindings, complete stage accounting, retained request evidence |
| V1 proposal | Audited quality errors, measured difficulty diagnostics, proposed source/cluster weights |

After v0 is runnable, use online Snowball success, cost, and learning-progress
signals to adjust sampling weights. Retain exploration weight and snapshot each
sampler change. Online adaptation, a full-corpus filter, and any training launch
are subsequent experiments; this proposal does not claim their results.

Implementation: [canonical ingester and runtime support #10319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10319), following the existing curation catalog and TaskCompendium converter pattern; [trainer companion draft](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032). The canonical converter reproduces all 11,634 selected native TaskSpecs byte-for-byte. Package publication, trainer lock updates, and actual inference remain release gates.

spillover_issues.author: raspberryice
spillover_issues.body:
> Context: 
> I've been running some IF training experiments on my own and noticed that that Nemotron RLVR1 blend checker has issues and the model is prone to reward hacking such as producing non-sense answers or language switching to circumvent constraints. Since the same dataset was used in Snowball RL training, I'm reporting the issue here to raise awareness about IF training set quality issues. 


_Some instruction-following (IF) rows in the Nemotron RLVR1 blend reward answers that ignore the request (all caps, Title Case, no Latin letters, or a non-Latin script), score at random, or cannot be passed._ 

[Cleaned-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) has 1,142 such rows among its 11,817 IF rows. Cleaned-v3 is the training set of the Antidoom RLVR1 v2 run, which produced Antidoom RLVR1 Step12, and of its Reference-KL continuation, which produced Reference-KL Step20 (#9735). The PivotRL mixed-RLVR arms (#10214) also train with its IF rows in the mix (#10215). Snowball v0.1 (Smartie run `.32`, #10305) trained on no IF constraint rows, but it started from the Campaign 2 merge, whose parents include Antidoom Step12 and Reference-KL Step20 (#9975).

| Constraint | Rows | Prompt text | NVIDIA checker |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `count:lowercase_counting` | 869 | "all lowercase words should appear at most N times", N = 2 or 3 | Allows at most N lowercase words in the whole answer, so only all-caps, Title Case or non-Latin answers pass ([instructions.py:2348](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2348)) |
| `letters:letter_counting` with `relation: "less than"` | 203 | "Answer with less than N letters", N = 2 or 3 | Passes only answers with fewer than N Latin letters, such as `42` ([instructions.py:2355](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2355)) |
| `length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word` with `nth_paragraph = num_paragraphs + 1` | 77 | "There should be 3 paragraphs. ... Paragraph 4 must start with word feedback." | Replaces the out-of-range `nth_paragraph` with `randint(1, num_paragraphs + 1)` on every call, so the paragraph it checks is random ([instructions.py:929](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L929)) |
| `count:counting_composition` | 1 | "delimited by the markdown divider: * * *" | Splits paragraphs only on `***`, so an answer that uses the prompt's `* * *` divider fails ([instructions.py:2440](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2440)) |

Eight rows carry two of these constraints.

Antidoom RLVR1 v2 and Reference-KL graded IF rows with MarinSkyRL's [`grade_instruction_following`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/instruction_following.py#L61-L84). It runs NVIDIA's pinned `verifiable_instructions@f46a5ac` checks and returns 1.0 only when every constraint passes. Its paragraph patch ([L54-L57](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/instruction_following.py#L54-L57)) applies only when `nth_paragraph` is missing, and the 77 rows set it. MarinSkyRL's opt-in verifyit path rejects those 77 rows at preparation ([instruction_verifyit.py:242](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/instruction_verifyit.py#L242)). It is off by default ([env.py:80](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/env.py#L80)), and I found no setting that enables it in the Antidoom RLVR1 v2 run notes or the Reference-KL config. The reward does not check that the answer addresses the request. It also does not check the answer's language, so a non-Latin answer passes `lowercase_counting` on an English prompt. 3,166 of the 11,817 IF prompts (26.8%) contain CJK characters.

The task-curation grader on main (#10077) checks these constraints with verifyit, then asks a GLM-5.3 judge whether the answer addresses the request ([graders.py:316-378](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/graders.py#L316-L378)). verifyit's `count:lowercase_counting` passes answers with at least N lowercase words ([ifeval.py:547-552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L547-L552)), which inverts the prompt. Its `nth_paragraph_first_word` check fails every answer to the 77 off-by-one rows ([ifeval.py:143-155](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L143-L155)), so a run trained on this grader gives every sample on those rows reward 0. The GLM-5.3 judge scores the 203 `letter_counting` rows instead of a letter count.

11,688 of the 11,817 Cleaned-v3 IF rows appear verbatim in [`nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-2-RL-data`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-2-RL-data) `IF-RL/train.jsonl`. 

**Our observations:** 
In a GRPO run of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on that file, scored with open-instruct's IFEvalG checkers (whose `lowercase_counting` rule matches NVIDIA's), the `lowercase_counting` pass rate rose from 0.21 at step 0 to 0.96 at step 199. From step 79 on, 85–93% of those passes were mostly CJK (more than 20% CJK characters). Mostly-Chinese answers to English IFEval prompts went from 0% at step 0 to 34.5% at step 199, and `lowercase_counting` is one of the constraints that paid for them. I have not re-scored Snowball's logged IF rollouts, so I do not know whether its runs took these shortcuts. 

In our later runs, we excluded these rows and added two checks to the reward. A language check scores an answer 0 when more than 20% of its characters are CJK and the prompt has no CJK characters and no language:response_language constraint. With it, mostly-CJK answers that would otherwise have passed never exceeded 0.42% of all answers. We then required a Qwen3-32B judge to confirm that each constraint pass attempts the request before it scores 1, the same role as the GLM-5.3 judge in the task-curation grader. 

Reproduce:

1. Download `data/train.parquet` from Cleaned-v3 and count the affected rows:

   ```python
   import collections, json
   import pyarrow.parquet as pq

   info = pq.read_table("train.parquet", columns=["extra_info"]).column("extra_info").to_pylist()
   rows = [json.loads(i["nemotron_ultra"]["record_json"]) for i in info
           if i["nemotron_ultra"]["agent"] == "instruction_following_simple_agent"]


   def shortcuts(row):
       found = set()
       for name, kw in zip(row["instruction_id_list"], row["kwargs"]):
           kw = kw or {}
           if name == "length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word" and (kw.get("nth_paragraph") or 0) > kw["num_paragraphs"]:
               found.add("nth_paragraph_first_word off by one")
           elif name == "letters:letter_counting" and kw.get("relation") == "less than":
               found.add("letter_counting less than")
           elif name in ("count:lowercase_counting", "count:counting_composition"):
               found.add(name)
       return found


   flagged = [shortcuts(r) for r in rows]
   print(len(rows), sum(map(bool, flagged)), collections.Counter(c for f in flagged for c in f))
   # 11817 1142 Counter({'count:lowercase_counting': 869, 'letter_counting less than': 203,
   #   'nth_paragraph_first_word off by one': 77, 'count:counting_composition': 1})
   ```

2. Run NVIDIA's checks, after `pip install "verifiable-instructions @ git+https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions.git@f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf"`:

   ```python
   from verifiable_instructions import instructions_registry


   def build(name, **kwargs):
       checker = instructions_registry.INSTRUCTION_DICT[name](name)
       return checker, checker.build_description(**kwargs)


   lower, _ = build("count:lowercase_counting", N=3)
   lower.check_following("THE INTEGRAL IS FOUND BY SUBSTITUTION.")  # True
   lower.check_following("The integral is found by substitution.")  # False
   letters, _ = build("letters:letter_counting", N=2, relation="less than")
   letters.check_following("42")  # True
   for _ in range(4):  # the paragraph number in the description changes between builds
       print(build("length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word", num_paragraphs=3, nth_paragraph=4, first_word="feedback")[1])
   ```

3. Run verifyit's check:

   ```python
   from verifyit.modes.ifeval import CONSTRAINTS

   check = CONSTRAINTS["count:lowercase_counting"]
   check("The integral is found by substitution.", {"N": 3})  # (True, 'lower_words=5 need>=3')
   check("THE INTEGRAL IS FOUND BY SUBSTITUTION.", {"N": 3})  # (False, 'lower_words=0 need>=3')
   ```

Expected: no IF training row rewards all-caps, letterless or random answers, and verifyit's `count:lowercase_counting` implements its prompt text. If verifyit's check is changed to match the prompt, it will reward all-caps answers on the 869 `lowercase_counting` rows as NVIDIA's checker does, so those rows also need to be excluded or rewritten.

spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
Build an immutable 100,000-task candidate curriculum for fast-turnaround Snowball RL. Version `2026.10.19.2` contains 88,366 production-admitted TaskSpecs and 11,634 reviewed historical native closure imports. The [private browser](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/e2bd5c9d-0f93-4ce9-b7af-3c78ca55e5d1/v/2/) contains the complete selected pool; sign in with a work Google account.

The approved recipe targets equal shares across five families: 20,000 each. Calendar capacity is 9,115, so its shortfall is distributed over the other four families. Final counts are calendar 9,115; competitive coding 22,722; Reasoning Gym 22,721; STEM 22,721; structural 22,721. This supersedes the initial proposal to reuse [Ben's intended one-sixth/four plus one-third structural weights](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fed5a9383b92acacbe264c7e601e93d8437218d3/experiments/post_training/smartie/mixture-v2.json).

Sources:

- Calendar: Nemotron calendar and two Task Trove calendar datasets.
- Coding: Nemotron competitive coding, Eurus2, and verified Glaive sandboxes.
- Reasoning Gym: Nemotron puzzles and standalone Reasoning Gym.
- STEM: Nemotron STEM MCQA and OpenScience.
- Structural: all 11,087 selected admitted structured-output tasks plus 11,634 of Ben's synthetic structural-compliance tasks.

The 12 admitted sources have 244,938 eligible contracts after known holdout exclusions. Ben's pinned structural training release adds 57,364 native rows; full-contract deduplication removes 52, leaving 57,312 eligible. Combined candidate population: 302,250. Native additions are sampled as evenly as possible across eight structural families, then their control strata; no row is repeated to fill a quota. Distinct private grading contracts remain distinct and all selected source aliases are retained.

Inputs are pinned in the export:

- Production catalog `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production`, snapshot `8c5d247ef6c2416fb3d14b2f159f74c4`; admitted `final/part-*.parquet` identities resolve through the verified CoreWeave migration receipt.
- [Exact historical native data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3), with file hashes, native validation IDs and tokenizer-aware prompt identities.
- Four evaluation sources and the known 910-task native validation panel. Native holdout checks use effective token prompts and full contracts, not their shared generic instruction text.

Done when:

- [x] Freeze source revisions, admission/import status, holdouts, recipe, and replay code.
- [x] Exclude known exact holdout overlap; deduplicate complete contracts and retain source aliases.
- [x] Select deterministically without replacement, recording quotas, probability denominators and provisional difficulty labels.
- [x] Publish 100,000 selected contracts, rejection accounting, Parquet, original payloads, readiness, and hashes.
- [x] Implement the historical native closure adapter and validate exact prompts and grading through the current CPU engine/trainer.
- [ ] Publish/pin the updated runtime libraries and trainer, resolve canonical external grader dependencies, and validate actual inference before declaring the complete pool training-ready.

Immutable export: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/2026.10.19.2`. Its verified-copy completion manifest covers 20 files, 3,812,705,369 bytes. All published payload hashes match the frozen artifact manifest. Predecessor `2026.10.19.1` remains available unchanged.

Independent validation confirms 100,000 unique task IDs and full contracts, exact family quotas, source/stratum probabilities, retained aliases, and zero known exact holdout overlap. Retained canonical TaskSpec JSON strings are byte-identical to the same task records in the verified predecessor; native payload strings match the pinned historical release. Parquet round trips preserve both formats byte-for-byte. Twenty focused tests, scoped repository lint, and Pyrefly pass. Implementation is tracked in the linked ingester/runtime and trainer PRs.

The immutable pool retains original historical payloads. In its `train.parquet`, `contract_kind` selects either `task_json` or `lowered_task_spec`; the unused payload is null. A separate native adapter now emits 11,634 current `TaskRolloutSpec` records in the trainer’s `task_rollout_spec` column. All selected native tasks passed reference/invalid completions through the current CPU engine (23,268 attempts); all 88,366 canonical identities remain unchanged. The native export passed the actual trainer dataset, and scripted workers covered all eight native families. This is local source/CPU evidence. Published runtime-library releases and trainer lock updates remain release gates. For the smoke, the three adapter packages use exact Git revisions and a separately published full 100,000-task deployment pool. It remaps only the package-lock URI in 51,915 script tasks to a derived historical environment; the expired original dirty-build environment cannot be reconstructed exactly. The remaining 48,085 task payloads, including all native tasks, remain unchanged. The live Linux CPU gate validated the complete pool and returned grades for ten sandbox probes. The requested ten-step GPU smoke then failed on both attempts during Megatron Bridge’s pipeline-group metadata gather, before any optimizer step or verified policy inference. The exact runtime failure and diagnostic proposal are recorded below. Difficulty remains a source/family prior; exact holdout exclusions do not establish semantic decontamination.

The approved derived native component is published at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/native-runtime/2026.10.19.1`: nine files, 8,473,539 bytes. Independent full readback matches every frozen SHA-256 and size. Its Parquet contains 11,634 native tasks and does not replace the full 100,000-task pool.

Related: [10k quality/annotation pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), [design #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Implementation: [canonical ingester and runtime support #10319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10319), following the existing curation catalog and TaskCompendium converter pattern; [trainer companion draft](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032). The canonical converter reproduces all 11,634 selected native TaskSpecs byte-for-byte. Package publication, trainer lock updates, and actual inference remain release gates.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The converted release has 4,997,251 training instances, but those counts precede admission, holdout exclusion, and contract deduplication. The four exact NVIDIA components have 13,023 converted instances against roughly 66,667 nonstructural slots in the intended mixture; the structural pool also needs a separate pin. The issue reports no materialized pool, and I could not verify admitted counts without the CoreWeave catalog credentials.

**Relevant code**
- [`catalog_snapshot.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/catalog_snapshot.py) — catalog snapshot selection
- [`task_curation/README.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/README.md) — admitted output and publication contract
- [TaskSpec input PR #10066](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10066) — trainer input boundary
- [runtime PR #10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) — current-stack smoke dependency

# Proposed Fix

Follow the selection policy in [#10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316), with these deliverables in order:

1. In the data region, resolve the converted manifest, `production` catalog, each source's admitted `final/part-*.parquet`, holdout IDs, and structural pool to immutable revisions and hashes. Publish an eligibility census by source before choosing expansion sources.
2. Freeze a recipe listing every added source ID and family. Exclude evaluation and known holdout overlap; group identical task and verifier contracts with the existing TaskCompendium identity mechanism. Report eligible counts and rejection reasons, including sources with no admitted rows.
3. Implement and fixture-test seeded selection without replacement: family weights `1/6, 1/6, 1/6, 1/6, 1/3`; square-root weighting across sources in a family; caps and redistribution; and equal coverage of nonempty difficulty strata, retaining `unknown` and provenance. Emit an explicit shortfall if 100,000 unique eligible tasks are unavailable.
4. Publish immutable TaskSpecs, selected identities, source aliases, quotas versus actual counts, rejection accounting, and artifact hashes. Re-run the selector against the same pins to verify identical output.
5. After the TaskSpec input and runtime ports are usable, load the pool on the current stack and smoke roughly 100 distinct tasks covering every selected execution and grader contract. Quarantine failing contracts, reselect, and retain reset/step/grading traces before declaring the pool ready.

The source expansion list, structural-pool pin, and CoreWeave access are prerequisites for the real census and release. The open [#10066](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10066) and [#10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190) PRs cover adjacent input/runtime work; I found no open PR materializing this pool.
